articles.title: What happened to Jaylen Harrell? Police reveal alleged Uber driver assault before Titans star’s crash
articles.summary: Tennessee Titans defensive end Jaylen Harrell is facing questions after a serious car accident in Tampa, Florida, left him hospitalized with major
articles.body: Tennessee Titans defensive end Jaylen Harrell is facing questions after a serious car accident in Tampa, Florida, left him hospitalized with major injuries. According to the Tampa Police Department, the 24-year-old allegedly assaulted his Uber driver while riding in the back seat on Friday morning, November 20. Police say the driver lost control after the reported incident, hitting another vehicle before crashing into a utility pole. Harrell struck his head against the windshield and lost consciousness. The incident is now under investigation, while the NFL player remains in the hospital.Tampa Police Reveal What Happened Before Jaylen Harrell's Serious Car AccidentThe accident took place on Friday morning while Harrell was travelling in a white Kia Sorento rideshare vehicle in his hometown of Tampa.According to a statement from the Tampa Police Department obtained by the Daily Mail, Harrell was sitting in the back seat when he reportedly assaulted the driver while the vehicle was moving.Police said the driver, a man in his mid-30s, swerved after the alleged incident. The Kia then struck another vehicle before hitting a utility pole. The impact sent Harrell forward into the windshield. He hit his head and lost consciousness.The rideshare driver suffered minor injuries and received treatment at the scene. The driver of the second vehicle, a woman in her early 50s who was driving a Toyota Highlander, escaped without injuries.Harrell, however, was taken to a nearby hospital with serious injuries. Police said he remained under medical care. The department has not shared further details about his condition or explained what may have led to the alleged assault.The investigation is still active. Police are looking into the events that took place inside the vehicle before the crash. No further details about possible charges have been confirmed.Tennessee Titans Share Update on Jaylen Harrell's Hospital ConditionThe Tennessee Titans also released a statement on Saturday, November 21, confirming that Harrell was still receiving medical care. However, the team did not mention the police allegations or provide details about what happened before the crash.The statement read:"Yesterday, Jaylen Harrell was involved in a serious car accident that resulted in him being taken to the hospital in his hometown of Tampa, Florida."We have been in constant communication with Jaylen's family and are still working to gather more information."At this time, Jaylen remains in the hospital and continues to receive care. We ask that Jaylen and his family's privacy be respected at this time. We will provide an update when appropriate."The team's statement came as Harrell was already dealing with a difficult season. He has not played a single game for Tennessee in 2026 after tearing his ACL during the preseason. The injury forced the Titans to place him on season-ending injured reserve in August.Harrell joined the Titans as a seventh-round pick in the 2024 NFL Draft. Before entering the NFL, he played college football for the Michigan Wolverines and was part of the team that won the national championship following the 2023 season.The 24-year-old appeared in all 34 regular-season games during his first two NFL seasons. He started two of those games and recorded 38 combined tackles, seven tackles for loss, 4.5 sacks and one forced fumble.His absence had already kept him away from the field this season. Now, the crash has raised further concerns about his health, while the police investigation has brought a separate issue into focus.As of Sunday, November 22, the Titans had not announced any further update on Harrell's condition. The team has also not publicly addressed the allegations made in the police statement.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

4. Jacksonville Jaguars (7-3, AFC South)

Amid their absence from the playoffs and a disastrous end to the 2025 season, the rest of the NFL slept on the Kansas City Chiefs entering this year. A sputtering offense earlier in the season did not help matters.

Kenneth Walker's work at running back, the emergence of Emmett Johnson in the backfield, and a trade for Josh Downs have sparked the offense, while Patrick Mahomes is starting to look like the face of this generation of quarterbacks that he was two seasons ago.

The three-time Super Bowl champion and MVP has thrown 13 touchdowns and no interceptions over the last four games. Two of them were to Travis Kelce on Sunday in Sunday afternoon's rout of the Arizona Cardinals, 34-7.

In the team's last three victories, they have allowed an average of 10.6 points, thanks to a defense finding its stride.

There is an argument to be made that the team has not played a particularly strong schedule, with their two losses coming against winning teams in Denver and Seattle, but a team can only play who is in front of them.

The Chiefs have done that to great success.

With games against the Bills, Rams, and Bengals on the slate over the next three weeks, we will find out if this Chiefs team is for real or a pretender, thriving on one of the easier schedules in the league through the first 11 weeks.

articles.title: NFL defends incomplete pass ruling on Parker Washington's would-be TD in Jaguars' loss at Giants
articles.summary: (AP) — Parker Washington thought he caught the ball for a crucial touchdown in the fourth quarter, and Jacksonville Jaguars coach Liam Coen was confident eno...
articles.body:
EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. (AP) — Parker Washington thought he caught the ball for a crucial touchdown in the fourth quarter, and Jacksonville Jaguars coach Liam Coen was confident enough that he challenged the initial call of an incomplete pass.

The league defended its decision after the Jaguars lost 23-18 at the New York Giants on Sunday, ruling that Washington did not complete the catch.

"It was determined that the receiver did not gain full control of the ball until he was out of bounds," vice president of instant replay Mark Butterworth told a pool reporter. "He needs to maintain control of the ball throughout the process of the catch."

Coen relayed that he was told "the ball switched hands.

"That was what it came down to," Coen said.

Washington felt good about possession but also did not want to blame the defeat on the officiating.

"I saw it on the Jumbotron or whatever we call it," Washington said. "It didn't go our way. You can't hang your head on that. We've got to move on and get ready for the next play."

Trevor Lawrence, who threw two interceptions while under pressure for much of the game, similarly did not want to lament the impact of the would-be touchdown on the result.

"It's a close play," Lawrence said. "Obviously, they called it and said it wasn't. It's tough. I thought it was incredible that he gave us a shot there and he caught it, and it looked like he had two feet down, but it was close. You can't leave in the refs' hands. I think it's a tough call for them."

CBS rules analyst Gene Steratore, who was an official in the league for 15 years, disagreed with the decision .

"I still had the right foot down as he's falling," Steratore said on the broadcast. "I see the ball move a little bit, but I did not think he lost possession of the football."

Giants coach John Harbaugh was fine with it, saying he thought simply "the ball moved."

articles.title: “I can’t worry about my personal feelings”: Jerry Jones keeps Christian Parker’s Dallas Cowboys comeback alive after Mike Pettine’s defensive changes deliver a stunning win over Titans
articles.summary: Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones has left the door open for Christian Parker to reclaim his defensive playcalling duties.
articles.body: Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones has left the door open for Christian Parker to reclaim his defensive playcalling duties. Mike Pettine took charge against the Tennessee Titans in Week 11 and helped Dallas secure a 51-30 victory. However, Jones does not seem ready to move on from Parker. His latest comments suggest the young defensive coordinator could still get another opportunity in Dallas.Jerry Jones hints at Christian Parker's return to Cowboys playcallingThe Cowboys made the coaching change after six losses in their first 10 games of the 2026 season. They took playcalling duties away from Parker and handed them to senior defensive assistant Mike Pettine. The move produced encouraging results against Tennessee, but Jones made it clear that Parker remains part of his plans.During the postgame show on 105.3 The Fan, Cowboys insider Bobby Belt shared Jones' response when reporters asked about Parker's future.“Christian Parker, I’d say it’s more a fact that he’ll be calling plays again in the NFL and maybe with the Dallas Cowboys,” Jones said, according to Belt.That comment is significant because Parker has not lost his defensive coordinator position. Pettine has simply taken over the playcalling responsibilities, while Parker continues to work with the defensive unit.Pettine also had a strong first outing. The Cowboys kept the Titans out of the end zone in the first half, allowed only three points during that period and recorded five sacks against quarterback Cam Ward.However, Tennessee still finished with 30 points. Dallas also extended its unwanted streak of allowing at least 20 points in 18 consecutive games.Christian Parker puts Cowboys ahead of personal feelings after demotionJones also discussed Parker's reaction during his appearance on 105.3 The Fan's K&C Masterpiece following the Week 11 victory.“I don’t have an issue, and I don’t think anybody else should if they know what I know,” Jones said.Parker had already addressed the situation during a press conference before the Titans game. Although he admitted that losing playcalling duties was difficult, he made it clear that he would not allow personal disappointment to affect the team.“It’s not an ideal situation for me personally, but it’s what’s best for the team at this current point,” Parker said.“I can’t worry about my personal feelings. I can’t worry about any of that. I’ve got to worry about the players. I’ve got to worry about the staff, to make sure that we handle business appropriately on Sunday. This isn’t gonna be a distraction.”His response appears to have impressed Jones, who believes Parker still has room to grow as a coach.Currently, Pettine will continue calling defensive plays as Dallas prepares for its Thanksgiving matchup against the Philadelphia Eagles on November 26. But Jones' comments offer Parker something valuable: the possibility of getting his old responsibilities back.The Cowboys now face an important stretch of their season, and their defensive performance will remain under scrutiny. If Pettine can maintain the improvement, Jones may have little reason to rush another change. However, Parker's experience and Jones' public backing mean his role in Dallas is far from settled. The coming weeks could offer a better picture of whether he gets another chance to call the defense.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Broncos' Bo Nix Campaigns for NFL Stats Rule Change for Hail Mary INTs, 'They Suck'
articles.summary: Bo Nix wants his pick nixed.
articles.body:
With the Denver Broncos up 17-10 a few seconds before halftime, head coach Sean Payton opted not to try a 68-yard field goal and instead, the Broncos quarterback Nix threw a Hail Mary, intercepted in the end zone by the Raiders.

He does not think that should count on his stat sheet.

"They suck," he told reporters during his postgame press conference.

"That's the play that's called and my job is to take a good drop, let them get down there, throw it. Hail Mary interceptions, they suck, to be honest with you. They're terrible, they put a bad taste in your mouth after a good first half."

That was the lone mark on his stats in a day when he threw for 225 yards and a touchdown in a 38-24 win over the Las Vegas Raiders.

"I think it should be like basketball, where if you chuck it from half-court it shouldn't count," Nix said. "But, that's just part of the game and definitely sucks to throw interceptions. I hate the stat, I can't stand putting it another tally in the stat sheet."

The Broncos are 8-2 after the win and have won six games in a row.

articles.title: 5 momentous plays in Week 11 include Ravens' mistakes, DK Metcalf's ejection and J.J. McCarthy's timely tackle
articles.summary: The Ravens made this list twice, plus those who were naughty (DK Metcalf) and nice (J.J. McCarthy).
articles.body:
In a "Momentous Plays" first, one team has snagged the top two spots this week. Take a bow, Baltimore Ravens.

They were hardly alone in the Hall of Ignominy on Sunday, joined by noted scofflaw DK Metcalf's latest affront .

Our final two momentous plays fall more into the "bad luck" and "great football play" categories, giving us a nice variety.

Here are the five most momentous plays from Sunday's early and afternoon games.

The Ravens coughed up Sunday's game in a colorful variety of ways. The first big shock was Justice Hill's brilliant run … which was capped by a gutting ending.

Baltimore led 12-7 and was deep in Carolina territory when Hill peeled off what appeared to be a 36-yard touchdown. But out of nowhere came Panthers cornerback Will Lee, who ripped the ball out at the final second. The fumble bounced out of the back of the end zone, giving the ball back to the Panthers in a shocking turn of events.

Replays showed just how close Hill was to the end zone when Lee saved the day. Panthers head coach Dave Canales later called the forced fumble one of his favorite plays of his tenure.

The Ravens forced a punt on the next series, but — get this — they muffed the punt, setting the Panthers up in glorious field position. A few plays later, the Panthers scored a touchdown, giving them the lead at 14-12.

It was basically a 14-point swing — but the Panthers' lead was short-lived, as the Ravens ran back the ensuing kickoff for a touchdown, putting them back ahead.

This easily could've been a Ravens blowout had a few plays gone differently early. And they weren't done yet!

A wild game that saw seven lead changes came down to the Ravens driving late and trailing 35-33 with just over a minute left. Even after all their mistakes, they had a chance to steal a road game and keep their dim playoff hopes alive.

Jacoby Brissett, who had a big game, was sacked with 1:30 remaining. About 25 seconds then ticked off the clock before he dumped a short pass to Hill, leading the Ravens to use their first timeout with 59 seconds remaining.

Brissett converted a fourth-and-1 sneak at his 31-yard line. The next snap came with 36 seconds left. The Ravens had three timeouts left at the start of the drive, and they had let almost a minute run off the clock to run four plays.

Again, they were at least 30 yards from field-goal range. It was putrid clock management, and it seemed to make the Ravens tighter as they tried to win.

Brissett's next pass was tipped by the omnipresent Lee and intercepted by Tyrel Dodson to seal a Panthers win. The Ravens' sixth straight loss would seem to make a late-season Lamar Jackson return even less likely.

3. DK's near eyepoke of Cooper DeJean is another eyesore for Steelers

DK Metcalf's latest misstep cost the Steelers on Sunday.

Metcalf drew two personal foul calls in Sunday's 19-16 loss at the Eagles , getting disqualified with just under five minutes remaining in the third quarter. The second penalty came after a third-and-8 incompletion, and Metcalf wasn't directly involved in the play, with the ball going in the direction of Germie Bernard.

Metcalf "just missed" poking the eye of the Eagles' Cooper DeJean, the Philadelphia defensive back told reporters postgame . He and Metcalf had been jawing all game to that point. The penalty pushed the Steelers back, though the immediate effect of his ejection wasn't felt, as Chris Boswell nailed the field goal to cut the Eagles' lead to 16-9.

Still, Metcalf left the game with one 2-yard reception and was gone for the remainder of a three-point Steelers loss. If there was a bright side, his absence gave an unexpected opportunity to Max Hurleman, who made multiple impressive catches, including a TD, in his NFL debut.

But with all due respect to Hurleman, for whom we're rooting, those catches should have been to the receiver the Steelers are paying $33 million per year.

The Buccaneers trailed 10-7 at halftime in Detroit. It appeared that Tampa Bay was about to take a second-half lead on its opening drive of the third quarter.

Irving ripped off an untouched 80-yard touchdown run, but the referees had other ideas. Luke Goedeke was flagged for holding, wiping out the play, and it appeared to be the right call, as Goedeke pulled the Lions defender to the ground.

Instead of a crowd-silencing TD, it was a first-and-long situation, backed up in Tampa's own end. Baker Mayfield's third-and-17 pass a few plays later came up a yard short, and the Bucs had to punt.

The Lions pushed the lead to 17-7 about three minutes later, with Jared Goff hitting Jameson Williams on a 57-yard bomb. The Bucs eventually cut the deficit to 17-14 before losing 31-21 in a game they never led.

J.J. McCarthy finished Sunday's win over the Jaguars with 173 yards passing, 33 more rushing, one touchdown pass and one critical tackle.

The Giants missed a field-goal try to open the second half, but their defense — which played great all game — forced the Jaguars to a three-and-out. Trying to pad a 20-6 lead, the Giants drove to the Jaguars' 32-yard line when disaster struck. Cam Skattebo coughed up a first-and-10 handoff, and Jaguars safety Antonio Johnson scooped it up.

Johnson had the look of a man trying to house it, continuing to look behind him for potential stalkers with a lot of green in front of him. But McCarthy raced over toward the sideline, and Johnson didn't appear to see him until it was too late. The QB took him down as the would-be free safety on the play.

The 42-yard return appeared to be the break the Jaguars needed, but it turned out that McCarthy's tackle saved seven points. The Jaguars turned the ball over on downs, and though the Giants couldn't immediately take advantage, saving the points was critical.

The Jaguars scored on three of their final four drives, and the Giants added only one more field goal, but McCarthy's tackle and Paulson Adebo's fourth-quarter interception of Trevor Lawrence were the massive plays the Giants needed to hang on.

articles.title: Mike Tomlin Reacts to DK Metcalf's Ejection for DeJean Altercation in Steelers' Loss to Eagles
articles.summary: DK Metcalf had a low moment on Sunday when the Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver was ejected from a matchup against the Philadelphia Eagles after receiving two unsportsmanlike penalty calls.
articles.body:
DK Metcalf had a low moment on Sunday when the Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver was ejected from a matchup against the Philadelphia Eagles after receiving two unsportsmanlike penalty calls.

Mike Tomlin, the former head coach of the Steelers who now works for NBC, weighed in on the ejection during Sunday Night Football's halftime show, giving some perspective from someone who knows Metcalf well.

"It's one thing to struggle in terms of production, and he certainly is struggling. But it's another thing to complicate it by showing a lack of professional maturity," Tomlin said. "And that's what he showed. He was frustrated, and so he did some things that are outside the lines of the game. And he certainly paid the consequence today, but he's probably going to continue to pay the consequence, whether it's from New York or whether it's in-house."

Metcalf received an unnecessary roughness penalty after getting into a shoving match with a handful of Eagles' players, and he was later ejected after seemingly trying to poke cornerback Cooper DeJean in the eye.

As Tomlin said, Metcalf has done nothing statistically to excuse his behavior on Sunday. He's recorded just 36 receptions for 434 yards and two touchdowns in 10 games.

Whether a further suspension for Metcalf is on the way remains to be seen.

articles.title: Josh Allen's wife Hailee Steinfeld has a holiday message that goes beyond gifts, parties and Christmas traditions
articles.summary: Hailee Steinfeld has turned her Beau Society newsletter into a holiday hosting guide, just as Thanksgiving, Friendsgiving and Christmas gatherings get
articles.body: Hailee Steinfeld has turned her Beau Society newsletter into a holiday hosting guide, just as Thanksgiving, Friendsgiving and Christmas gatherings get underway. The actress, who is married to Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen, filled her latest issue with reader advice on dinner parties, her favorite hostess gifts and a creamy chicken noodle soup recipe. The couple hosted a Halloween party not long ago, and this will be their first Christmas as parents to daughter Harper Haize Allen. Her message is simple, and it has little to do with presents: the season is about making people feel welcome.Hailee Steinfeld's holiday message goes beyond gifts, parties and traditionsMost of the advice came from readers, not from Steinfeld herself. She collected what regular hosts have learned over the years, and little of it costs money. That gives the list a lived-in feel.Music got plenty of attention. One reader suggested starting with softer songs as guests arrive, moving to jazz or acoustic music during dinner, and finishing the night with old favorites. It is an easy way to set the mood without making a show of it.Other tips were about people. Keep an extra chair nearby. Introduce guests who may not know each other. Don't rush anyone through dinner. All of them aim at the same problem: the guest who feels like an outsider at a table full of friends.Another reader pushed for a theme. One idea was a cozy Christmas night with pajamas and hot chocolate. Another was a Paris-inspired evening with French food and macarons. Neither needs a big budget, only a little planning, and both give a party a shape that a plain dinner can lack.The timing is good. Thanksgiving is just days away, and Christmas follows soon after. For Steinfeld and Allen, the season also carries extra weight. This is their first Christmas with Harper, and they plan to make it a special one.Hailee Steinfeld shares her favorite hostess gifts and a cozy soup recipeSteinfeld also spoke to the other side of the table. Being a good guest counts as much as being a good host, and she kept the rules short: bring a small gift, greet everyone when you arrive and offer to help clean up. None of that takes much effort, though it is easy to forget when the doorbell is ringing.For hostess gifts, she shared some favorites. Dessert plates, salted caramels, cocktail napkins, coffee table books and homemade treats all made the list. The mix is practical. Most of it can be picked up in a single stop, and the homemade option suits anyone who would rather bake than browse a store.Then came the soup. Steinfeld shared a recipe for creamy chicken noodle soup, which she recently made at home after feeding Harper. Her tip is to use half-and-half instead of whole milk. It gives the bowl extra creaminess.A recipe like that fits the tone of the whole newsletter. Nothing in it asks readers to host a flawless evening. A playlist, a spare chair and a pot of soup are enough to start with, and the rest comes from paying attention to the people in the room. That is a fair message for a holiday that often turns into a to-do list.Josh and Harper will be beside her for all of it. The Halloween party is behind them, and Christmas is next.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.body:
During the fourth quarter of Sunday's win against the Jacksonville Jaguars, New York Giants wide receiver Malik Nabers appeared to be upset about something on the sideline and was being held back by quarterback Jameis Winston.

Nabers addressed the situation after the game, saying that there was no tension between him and anyone on the sideline.

"I just remember me telling him, 'I'm good, I'm good. I want to get back to watching the defense play,'" Nabers said. "That was really all, I think... I was just telling the offense, 'Let's go.' Jameis was just kinda calming me down, but I was fine."

Nabers had a productive day with seven receptions for 55 yards and a touchdown, and it seems like he's still on good terms with his teammates after seeming frustrated about something during the game.

articles.title: NFL Says Parker Washington No-TD Call After Video Review Was Correct During Jaguars' Loss to Giants
articles.summary: Jacksonville Jaguars wide receiver Parker Washington appeared to make a crucial touchdown catch against the New York Giants on Sunday, but the officials ruled it a no-catch to negate the score.
articles.body:
Jacksonville Jaguars wide receiver Parker Washington appeared to make a crucial touchdown catch against the New York Giants on Sunday, but the officials ruled it a no-catch to negate the score.

Afterwards, NFL vice president of instant replay Mark Butterworth said on-field officials made the right call, per ESPN's Michael DiRocco . Washington got both of his feet in bounds, according to Butterworth, but he didn't have complete control of the ball when he hit the ground.

"He needs to maintain control of the ball throughout the process of the catch," Butterworth said.

"I felt good about it, but they said it wasn't a catch, so had to move on and finish that game," Washington said, per DiRocco. "I think he said I didn't maintain control. But it's OK. We're ready to move on."

Had it been ruled a touchdown, it would've trimmed the lead to just one score. Instead, the Jags had to settle for a field goal and a 20-9 deficit. The Giants went on to win 23-18.

Jacksonville dropped to 7-3 with the loss, but is still in full control of the AFC South. The Giants improved to 6-3-1 to maintain their lead in the NFC East.

articles.title: 49ers right tackle Colton McKivitz carted off in win over Vikings due to gruesome lower leg injury
articles.summary: McKivitz's left leg got pinned under multiple players at the end of a Christian McCaffrey run. When McKivitz pulled his leg from underneath the pile of playe...
articles.body:
San Francisco 49ers right tackle Colton McKivitz left Sunday's dominant win over the Minnesota Vikings due to what looked like a significant injury to his lower left leg.

The injury took place during the second quarter of the 35-10 win that was held in Mexico City . McKivitz's left leg got pinned under multiple players at the end of a Christian McCaffrey run.

When McKivitz pulled his leg from underneath the pile of players, his foot was twisted in the wrong direction.

Warning: Video below shows a graphic injury

McKivitz's teammates immediately knew he had sustained a significant injury. Multiple players took a knee around their injured teammate, and left tackle Trent Williams slammed his helmet into the turf, then held the back of his head in his hands.

Trainers rushed onto the field to tend to McKivitz. He was eventually taken off the field on a cart. He was upright and interacting with his teammates as they saw him off the field.

The nature of McKivitz's injury wasn't initially clear.

McKivitz is key to San Francisco's top-ranked offense. He's a strong run blocker who hasn't allowed a sack this season.

The 49ers have thrived despite injuries to key players on both sides of the ball this season, and Sunday night was no exception. They entered halftime with a 28-10 lead and cruised the rest of the way to secure the 25-point win. Brock Purdy went 21-of-26 for 255 yards with three touchdowns, two of which went to George Kittle.

They now sit at 9-1 on the season after the win, which marked their third straight.

articles.title: Brock Purdy Dazzles as 49ers Rout Vikings, Box Score Stats, Highlights for Cousins, CMC, Top Players
articles.summary: The San Francisco 49ers routed the Minnesota Vikings 35-10 in Mexico City on Sunday, behind an impressive performance from Brock Purdy, who threw for 255 yards and three touchdowns.
articles.body:
The San Francisco 49ers routed the Minnesota Vikings 35-10 in Mexico City on Sunday, behind an impressive performance from Brock Purdy, who threw for 255 yards and three touchdowns.

The 49ers entered the matchup as 3.5-point favorites, per FanDuel Sportsbook , and came away with a 25-point win, while holding Kirk Cousins without a touchdown pass and forcing an interception.

The win cemented the 49ers at the top of the NFC West, improving to 9-1 overall and 6-1 in conference play while extending their winning streak to three games.

Purdy continues to make his case for MVP, currently sitting second in the odds at +180 behind the Cincinnati Bengals' Joe Burrow at -125, per FanDuel Sportsbook .

The Vikings, meanwhile, dropped their first game with Cousins under center after opening his tenure with a 30-10 victory over the Green Bay Packers, falling to 7-3 and 5-2 in the conference.

The key was San Francisco cracking the Vikings' defense, becoming the first team this season to score 30 or more points against the No. 2-ranked defensive unit, which allows just 273.3 yards per game and leads the league in points allowed at 14.0 per game.

The 49ers opened the game with a 17-yard touchdown pass from Purdy to tight end George Kittle to take a quick 7-0 lead.

Minnesota had a chance to take the lead after the first quarter, but missed a 55-yard field goal before Aaron Jones Sr. found the end zone to tie things up at seven heading into the second quarter.

San Francisco erupted in the second quarter with three touchdowns, as Purdy found Kittle for his second score and connected with Mike Evans before Ji'Ayir Brown intercepted Cousins and returned it for a pick-six. The 49ers scored 21 points in the quarter to take a 28-10 lead into halftime.

Purdy entered halftime 10-of-12 passing for 166 yards and three touchdowns in an explosive first half.

The score remained unchanged in the third quarter despite a fumble by Vikings wide receiver Justin Jefferson, as the 49ers could not capitalize on the miscue.

Christian McCaffrey scored his first touchdown of the evening to open the fourth quarter, giving the 49ers a commanding 25-point lead that would hold on for the win.

San Francisco will host the Seattle Seahawks next Sunday at 4:25 p.m. ET, while the Vikings will host the Atlanta Falcons at 1 p.m. ET the same day.

articles.title: Fernando Mendoza 'Felt A Lot More Comfortable' in 2nd Career NFL Start, Talks Raiders vs. Broncos
articles.summary: Despite a 38-24 loss to the Denver Broncos on Sunday, Las Vegas Raiders rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza said he felt better in his second career NFL start.
articles.body:
Despite a 38-24 loss to the Denver Broncos on Sunday, Las Vegas Raiders rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza said he felt better in his second career NFL start.

"I felt a lot more comfortable than last week," Mendoza told reporters in his postgame press conference. "I was able to settle in and able to see the entire field better."

Mendoza threw 18-for-37 with 267 yards and three touchdowns in his second start since the Raiders traded their previous starting quarterback, Kirk Cousins, to the Minnesota Vikings.

He was also sacked five times and threw an interception near the end of the contest.

He also noted that the crowd in Denver was loud and caused some communication issues.

Mendoza was the No. 1 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft and is clearly the Raiders' quarterback of the future, so his growing comfort is a good sign for them and him.

"If you just do your job, your momentum is going to swing your way eventually," Mendoza said.

articles.title: MVP Brock Purdy? 49ers next Super Bowl champions? It's all on the table now for San Francisco
articles.summary: San Francisco threw around Minnesota on Sunday night, and the road to the Super Bowl is wide open now for the 49ers.
articles.body:
For millennia, philosophers and professors have pondered an impossible question: What happens when an irresistible force meets an immovable object? Well, we have our answer, and we didn't even need AI to solve it: Irresistible Force knocks out Immovable Object by 25 points .

San Francisco and Minnesota arrived in Mexico City at the absolute pinnacles of the NFL's two barometers of excellence. No team in the NFL gains more yards per play than the 49ers. No team sacks quarterbacks more than Minnesota. Dominating offense, smothering defense. Irresistible force, immovable object.

The 49ers strode onto the field at Estadio Azteca and proceeded to stomp all over the Vikings. San Francisco set the tone with a seven-play, 72-yard opening drive that finished in the end zone in less than four minutes. The Vikings immediately struck back with a touchdown.

And then, like a street fighter wiping a drop of blood off his lip before administering a generational beatdown, the 49ers blew away the league's top scoring defense with a total of 35 points, through the air and on the ground. And if you could score touchdowns by water, well, the 49ers probably would have done that too. This was a statement win carved into the side of a mountain, a declaration that the road to the Super Bowl runs through San Francisco.

At 9-1, the 49ers lead the the NFC West by three games and the NFC as a whole by a game, and stand even with the Bills for the best record in the NFL. Aside from an inexplicable loss to the Falcons — who probably won't get another shot at the 49ers this season — San Francisco has overwhelmed its opposition at every turn.

If there's anything that can slow this 49ers team, it's the blue medical tent. Injuries have ravaged the 49ers all season, and on Sunday night, San Francisco ran out a Geriatric Avengers of thirty-somethings including George Kittle, Mike Evans, Christian McCaffrey, Deebo Samuel Sr. and Kyle Juszczyk. All that experience gives the 49ers a big-game-pressure edge that few teams can match, but it also makes them intensely vulnerable to injury. Stints on the IR are a when, not an if, for the 49ers. Right tackle Colton McKivitz was the latest as he suffered a gruesome leg injury in the first half Sunday night.

The guy ensuring all those uncs get the ball is finally receiving some attention of his own again, too. Brock Purdy hasn't shown up on MVP leaderboards since finishing fourth in his breakout season of 2023. This season ought to change that. He's among the league leaders in touchdowns, passer rating and completion percentage, among other useful stats.

Against the best defense in the NFL, all Purdy did was throw for three touchdowns and 255 yards on 21-of-26 completions. He's grown into the perfect weapon for head coach Kyle Shanahan's unorthodox offense, and Sunday was the perfect showcase.

"Brock, he didn't get rattled, which he really never does," Shanahan said after the game. "It's not like it's something new today to me with Brock. Brock's been like this since Day 1, and he's played at a very high level for a number of years now."

Purdy and Shanahan wisely used the Vikings' vicious aggressiveness against them. The NFL Next Gen Stats chart of Purdy's completions tells the tale ; virtually all of his completions were within 10 yards of the line of scrimmage, meaning he got rid of the ball so quickly that Minnesota couldn't catch up. You can't record a sack when the ball's already downfield.

"He just has this aura in the huddle," said Kittle, who caught Purdy's first two touchdown passes. "Everybody locks eyes with him, and we know every play, we have the chance to do something special."

"He's the best player in the game right now. He's super dialed in, the way he prepares, the way he competes," said Evans, who caught Purdy's third touchdown pass of the night, late in the first half. "He's tough. I always thought he's been underrated — his precision. Super-smart player."

This 49ers team is something special, and not just because it has managed to win in three countries and two hemispheres this season. The Niners are in the meat of their schedule now; the Seahawks, Rams and Chiefs all await over the next five weeks. So too do teams like the Chargers, Eagles and Cardinals; San Francisco's schedule ranks 23rd in the NFL in terms of remaining difficulty, per Tankathon .

"We're halfway through this year. We've done some good things, but I mean, [the Super Bowl is] still to be determined," Shanahan said. "We know how we've been so far, but we're halfway there and we've got a long way to go."

Shanahan has led his teams to within sight of the promised land, reaching the Super Bowl as a head coach or coordinator on three separate occasions. In all three, the Lombardi Trophy eluded him. There's no reason to expect that this season will be any different … except for the fact that there was no reason to expect San Francisco would throw around the best defense in the league, either. The Irresistible Force rolls on.

articles.title: As Liam Coen explains Jaguars' late field-goal decision, Giants take offense: 'Disrespectful as hell'
articles.summary: A pressure-happy Giants defense kept Trevor Lawrence from ever finding a rhythm.
articles.body:
EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. — Down eight points with 3:43 to play, the Jacksonville Jaguars faced fourth-and-goal from the 8-yard line.

Head coach Liam Coen checked his charts.

Should he bank on his offense, which converted just once on six red-zone trips Sunday, to reverse course amid unfavorable down-and-distance? Or should the Jaguars kick the 26-yard field goal, narrow their deficit to five points and trust the defense that held the New York Giants to three points in the second half to get a stop?

"Fourth-and-8 … what are those percentages of success? I think they're probably less than 5 [percent] in a lot of ways in this league … " Coen said after the game. "Just executing that down-and-distance on a fourth down is kind of challenging, especially when they are zero-blitzing every play. The ball's going to come out. It's like a 'hope' play."

So the Jaguars kicked the field goal and the Giants ran out the clock with two first downs. The Giants won 23-18 after leading for the final 47 minutes .

The Jaguars' strategy of relying on their defense during a day their offense struggled to maintain rhythm did not work out for the visiting team. But the strategy worked well to motivate a Giants team that had lost its own rhythm after halftime.

If the Jaguars thought the Giants weren't going to realize the message their field goal sent, they were mistaken. New York quarterback J.J. McCarthy said "as an offense, we took that personal" as Jacksonville hedged on yet another New York implosion.

"One hundred percent, it's disrespectful as hell," right tackle Jermaine Eleumenor said from the postgame locker room. "You're kicking a field goal, you think you're going to get a stop on defense, and if I'm being honest, we were whooping them. On the line of scrimmage, they weren't winning. We won the line of scrimmage, both sides of the ball."

On a day in which the Jaguars were down starting center Robert Hainsey (knee) and lost starting left tackle Walker Little (knee) early in the fourth quarter, a pressure-happy Giants defense kept Trevor Lawrence from ever finding a rhythm.

And on a day in which the Jaguars were onboarding their trade-deadline acquisition starting defenders in defensive tackle Jordan Davis and safety Jessie Bates III, the Giants capitalized on a group adjusting to complex schemes, including with quarterback keepers that powered each of their touchdown drives.

So consider the Giants aware that they were 6-point betting underdogs at home and aware that plenty questioned their division-leading record on account of the below-.500 teams they had beaten.

Giants head coach John Harbaugh called his team's sixth victory "the first real football win."

Edge rusher Abdul Carter said "everybody pretty much counted us out."

"But we took that as disrespect, and we came out with a chip on our shoulder … " said Carter, who finished the game with 2 sacks, 5 quarterback hits and 8 pressures, per Pro Football Focus. "I think we proved that we are worthy. They keep saying we can't beat these teams, we can't beat them. I don't know why they're saying that.

Lawrence on Giants defense: 'They punched us in the mouth'

At the end of the first quarter, the Jaguars had not scored a touchdown.

At the end of the second and then third, they hadn't either.

This was a Jacksonville team that entered the week averaging 29.9 points per game, fourth in the league. Its 358.9 yards per game ranked ninth in total offense. So what explained the 20-6 deficit that trickled into the fourth quarter?

"I played really, really poorly today, and you're not going to win many games if I don't play better than that … " said Lawrence, who more than doubled his first three quarters' output with a 164-yard fourth quarter that brought his day to 301 yards, 1 touchdown and 2 interceptions on 25-of-47 (53.2%) passing. "As an offense as a whole, I thought we didn't come out with the aggressiveness and attacking that we normally have.

"I felt like they punched us in the mouth a little bit."

Coen blamed himself for some of his early play-calling, saying he overcompensated for run calls he regretted a week prior by calling three straight passes to set up the opening drive's field goal. The Jaguars strayed on multiple drives from their run, which typically sets up their play-action passing and sets the tone for their physical offensive style. On third-and-medium-to-longs, the Giants pressured Lawrence to the tune of turnovers, incompletions and sacks.

Facing third-and-6 with 7:45 to play in the first quarter, Lawrence thought he could hit receiver Parker Washington out of reach of cornerback Deonte Banks before realizing it was "just a really bad read, really bad decision."

With 11:08 to play in the fourth quarter, Lawrence aimed to throw high and early to avoid an approaching defensive lineman, instead throwing to a spot receiver Jakobi Meyers had yet to reach.

The Giants turned the interceptions into six total points on a day they won by five.

Yet when Jacksonville safety Antonio Johnson stripped running back Cam Skattebo and returned the fumble 42 yards, the Jaguars' offense responded with a turnover on downs. Complementary football eluded the team.

By the time Lawrence found a rhythm in the fourth quarter, hitting receiver Brian Thomas Jr. for an 18-yard touchdown on third-and-10 sandwiched between two field-goal drives, the Jaguars' defense was waning. Perhaps matters would have been different if the officials had ruled differently on Washington's fourth-quarter catch in which he got two feet down but didn't secure the ball without movement as he fell to the ground; but even Lawrence admitted: "It was close, and you can't leave it in the ref's hands."

The Giants celebrated holding onto a lead after letting their last contest slip away to the Washington Commanders in the final minute. Lawrence lamented that his offense's rally was too little, too late.

"It was nice to see the fight at the end of the game and that we were still able to have a shot, thanks to our defense," Lawrence said. "We let our defense down today. They got us a bunch of turnovers and gave us plenty of opportunities to win the game, and we didn't capitalize."

With playoff chances still strong, Jaguars say Super Bowl dreams 'are still intact'

At 6-3-1, the Giants maintained their grip on the NFC East even as the Cowboys improved to 5-6 with a 51-30 win over the Tennessee Titans . Next Gen Stats projects the Giants' chances of making the playoffs at 70% after the win.

The Jaguars, meanwhile, don't just remain atop the AFC South at 7-3. Thanks to their three-game lead in the division, they carry a 98% chance of making the playoffs, per Next Gen Stats.

So postseason contention is not a front-of-mind problem. Cleaning up the errors that the Giants exposed, however, is.

Less than two weeks after trading for Davis and Bates as indications of the belief in the 2026 Jaguars, Jacksonville coaches and executives continue to echo that message.

"They believe in this year and they believe that we can make a push to go to the Super Bowl," cornerback Jourdan Lewis told Yahoo Sports. "Those dreams are still intact, just getting accustomed to the guys and how we want to play and how to attack offenses and how they want to attack our system too. …

Instead, the Jaguars will continue working to acclimate Bates to split-safety looks that differ from his Atlanta responsibilities prior to the trade, and they'll work with Davis as he learns the nuances of coordinator Anthony Campanile's movement calls while remembering that gap integrity, physicality and winning in the trenches will always be the foundation for defensive-line success.

The Jaguars were quiet as they shuffled into the postgame locker room from a rainy MetLife Field. But as they showered and packed up for their flight home, their tone reflected focus more than despair.

There are holes to patch. There is time, in the seven remaining regular-season contests, to patch them.

"It's not the end of the world," Davis told Yahoo Sports of Coen's message. "We have to fix the issues. We have to take our medicine. We have to look ourselves in the mirror and then move forward the next week.

"You don't have time to dwell on your wins and losses in the previous week. You have to move on."

So on the Jaguars will move from their five-point loss and on they'll move from Coen's decision to kick a field goal with 3:43 remaining. That decision will motivate Jacksonville's offensive players to show their head coach next time that they're capable of beating blitzes and performing even when the down and distance doesn't favor them.

And the decision's failure will motivate Jacksonville's defense to shore up the assignments that ceded McCarthy a 19-yard completion up the middle and Skattebo a 5-yard run on second-and-5 to seal the win.

Several Jaguars players echoed their trust in Coen on that decision and beyond. And Lawrence, who said he struggled to read the field efficiently until late in the game, said he understood which part of those late-game analytics moments were in his control.

"It's not my decision at the end of the day," Lawrence said. "It's coach's, but I stand by him. We've got to make plays on first, second and third down so we have a chance to go for it not on fourth-and-7 or 8. It's just a tough down …

"We know who we are. We just didn't play well tonight. If you don't play well, you get beat."

articles.title: NFL 2026 playoff picture taking shape, Travis Kelce has a big day and Fernando Mendoza proves he belongs - NFL Sunday Review
articles.summary: NFL Sunday Review - we reflect on Week 11 in the NFL as Travis Kelce moved past Rob Gronkowski for touchdowns all-time among tight ends, Las Vegas Raiders' No 1 overall draft pick Fernando Mendoza gave evidence he belongs and the Pittsburgh Steelers look in danger in the AFC playoff race
articles.body:
The San Francisco 49ers (9-1) further asserted their dominance in the NFC with a thumping 35-10 victory over the Minnesota Vikings and their much-vaunted defense in Mexico City - the final International Series game of the season - while the Buffalo Bills (9-1) share the same record as the AFC top seeds, albeit they were far less convincing in their 26-9 dispatching of the one-win Miami Dolphins.

Josh Allen threw two interceptions to allow the Dolphins to hang around until the Bills pulled away late. He and the team will need to sharpen up for their mouthwatering Thanksgiving night meeting with the Kansas City Chiefs (8-2) - live on Sky Sports NFL from 1.20am, Friday - that could ultimately end up deciding where the road to the Super Bowl runs through in the AFC.

However, it's below the Bills and the Chiefs, and the 49ers on the other side of the conference divide, where things are really starting to get interesting.

The Denver Broncos (8-2) are also in the mix for top billing in the AFC, after claiming a sixth straight against the Las Vegas Raiders, while the Cincinnati Bengals (7-2) have the opportunity to match that mark with a Monday night victory at the Washington Commanders.

The Jacksonville Jaguars (7-3) stumbled at the New York Giants (6-3-1), whose impressive victory strengthened their grip on the NFC East division, which the Dallas Cowboys (5-6) are still in the hunt for after hanging 51 on the Tennessee Titans defense.

The Jaguars' loss was far from fatal, with the Titans, along with the Indianapolis Colts and the Houston Texans all floundering in their division, though the Pittsburgh Steelers' (6-4) shock loss at the Philadelphia Eagles might well have opened the door to the latter in the race for a wildcard berth.

The Texans, who started the season 0-4, now sit 4-6 and - after a meeting with a Baltimore Ravens team in the midst of a six-game losing streak - will likely have the opportunity to match the Steelers' record when the two teams meet in a fortnight, following Pittsburgh's tricky assignment against the Broncos where they'll try to avoid dropping three in a row.

Meanwhile, back in the NFC, the greatest intrigue lies in the NFC North and the four-way battle unfolding for the division, with the Detroit Lions (8-2), Chicago Bears (8-2), Vikings (7-3) - even with their chastening loss to the Niners - and Green Bay Packers (6-4) all currently playoff bound.

Mind you, they all have the looming threat of the wildcard-hunting Los Angeles Rams (6-4) and defending Super Bowl-champion Seattle Seahawks (6-4) from the NFC West.

It makes the Thanksgiving night clash between the Lions and Bears in Detroit - live on Sky Sports NFL from 6pm, Thursday - even more crucial.

See, 'football season (really does) start at Thanksgiving'.

Lost in amongst how historically bad their defense is - even the one-win Titans scored on five of their first six possessions, one week on from the 49ers managing to score 46 points and a staggering 584 yards against them - is how impressive their offense is, and needs to be!

The Cowboys are just the fourth team in NFL history to allow at least 20 points in each of their first 11 games and still win at least five of those games. They have allowed 20 points in 18 straight games dating back to Week 12 of last season.

But Dak Prescott threw four touchdown passes and ran in another score as Dallas found the end zone on each of their first six drives in their 51-30 thumping of the Titans to somewhat mask their continued defensive woes.

There's still teething issues as the No 1 overall draft picks eases his way into NFL life - most notably the game-sealing pick-six he threw that ensured he starts his career with back-to-back defeats in his first two starts. But there was a lot to like too.

Mendoza and the Raiders hung with the Broncos far longer than many expected, with it being just a one-score game when the rookie QB tossed that costly interception.

Prior to that, he completed 18 of 37 passes for 267 yards and three passing touchdowns - his first in the NFL.

"I felt more comfortable than last week," Mendoza admitted afterwards. "I was able to settle in and able to see the entire field better.

"If you just do your job, your momentum is going to swing your way eventually."

Are the Steelers in danger of dropping out of the AFC playoff picture?

It certainly looks like they're in trouble. The 19-16 reverse in Philadelphia not only was the Eagles' first win in eight games, it was the Steelers' second straight loss, with Aaron Rodgers, who turns 43 on December 2, looking every bit his age as he limped to 95 passing yards when going 17 of 20 in the first half.

That turned into 227 yards by the end of the game after some garbage-time stat-padding, but it's looking a little rough for the Steelers, who currently occupy the seventh and final playoff berth in the AFC and have a dire run of stellar defenses to come over the next three-week stretch in the Broncos, Texans and Jaguars.

Helping their cause is the fact that the AFC isn't exactly flush with challengers. The New England Patriots (5-5) are currently their closes rivals but they're in the midst of their own crisis with starting quarterback Drake Maye out for the year, then there's the Texans (4-6) and that's pretty much it.

Though Houston's record looks pretty ugly at the minute, they won nine straight from 3-5 to get into the playoffs last year, so are well capable of going on a run.

Their visit to Pittsburgh in two weeks' time could prove pivotal.

David Bailey: The New York Jets rookie edge rusher had two sacks in their win at the Los Angeles Chargers that broke their five-game losing streak, giving him nine-and-a-half sacks on the season to go with six forced fumbles, including one against the Chargers.

The No 2 overall draft pick generated five pressures, meaning he has now recorded 45 pressures this season, the third-most by a rookie defender through Week 11 since 2018, trailing only Jared Verse (50 in 2024) and Nick Bosa (49 in 2019).

Travis Kelce: The veteran Chiefs tight end had 74 receiving yards to go with two receiving touchdowns in their win over the Arizona Cardinals, his first game with multiple receiving touchdowns since Week 11 of the 2022 season against the Chargers.

The 37-year-old's eight-yard score on Kansas City's opening possession also saw him pass Rob Gronkowski into third place for the most total touchdowns (including playoffs) by a tight end in NFL history with 109.

Only Pro Football Hall of Famers Antonio Gates (118) and Tony Gonzalez (115) have scored more.

DK Metcalf: The Steelers receiver was ejected from their game in Philadelphia after committing two unsportsmanlike conduct penalties 10 offensive plays apart, with the second of those appearing to see him reach into Cooper DeJean's facemask and poke the defensive back near the eye, sparking a melee between the two teams.

The ejection is Metcalf's third for his career since his debut in 2019. That's tied with 49ers linebacker Dre Greenlaw for the most in the NFL during that span.

"It's emotional on a number of fronts," Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy said afterwards. "We lost a game, a tough game. You take all that in, and everything will be addressed. We can't have players getting ejected from games."

Tennessee Titans: "All gas, no brake" is Tennessee head coach Robert Saleh's much-quoted mantra.

Well, the Titans took that sentiment a touch too literally on Sunday with someone seemingly cutting the breaks as they went careering off a cliff against the Cowboys.

And the coach, renowned for his defensive acumen, was NOT happy about the performance as his defense let up 51 points.

"It was disgusting, embarrassing football," Saleh said afterwards. "That starts with me. I got to figure it out.

"We have no choice but to get better. It can't get any worse."

Player of the Weekend - Jeffery Simmons, DT, Chicago Bears

Jeffery Simmons has been everything the Bears could've hoped for following their blockbuster mid-season trade for the former Titans defensive tackle which saw Chicago cough up two first-round draft picks.

He was the standout from Dennis Allen's unrelenting defense in their victory over the New Orleans Saints in which Chicago racked up a season-high 23 quarterback pressures and six sacks - Simmons recording three of those, tying his career high in a single game.

In doing so, he also became the first Bears defensive tackled to have three sacks in a game since 2014, taking his tally to five in three games since arriving in Chicago.

This one had a bit of everything, with the Carolina Panthers and Baltimore Ravens combining for 68 points and seven lead changes. There were also five turnovers, two muffed punts, a kickoff return for a touchdown and a safety!

Ultimately though it was the Panthers who prevailed 35-33 on the back of Ryan Fitzgerald's game-winning 37-yard field goal inside the final two minutes, their second straight win seeing them back to .500 at 5-5 on the season and strengthening their hold on the NFC South, while the Ravens are left reeling a sixth defeat in a row.

Carolina rode QB Bryce Young and running back Chuba Hubbard to victory, the former throwing for 254 yards and two TDs (as well as an interception), and Hubbard tallying 120 yards on 27 carries and two scores. The defense also finally stepped up in the second half to limit Baltimore to only seven points after the interval.

articles.title: It was the NFL’s toughest test. Then the 49ers made it look easy.
articles.summary: The Minnesota Vikings’ defense was the NFL’s most difficult all season. Until they ran into the best team in the NFL so far, the San Francisco 49ers.
articles.body: During breaks in Sunday’s matchup against Minnesota, San Francisco 49ers players retreated to their sideline in Mexico City and were handed breathing masks connected to oxygen tanks. Facing the blitz-happy, havoc-inducing Vikings has had the effect of leaving opponents breathless all season. But even playing at 7,352 feet of elevation, San Francisco’s players barely looked to be breathing hard while blunting the NFL’s most dangerous defense. In its 35-10 win in Estadio Azteca, San Francisco took apart vaunted Minnesota while showing why the 49ers (9-1) remain a leading Super Bowl contender 11 weeks into the season. Under the charge of coordinator Brian Flores, Minnesota had blitzed on more than three-quarters of their downs; no other team had done it even half the time. Not coincidentally, the Vikings had allowed the league’s fewest points and its second-fewest yards, while becoming the NFL’s most difficult problem to solve. Until Sunday — when the Vikings ran into the league’s toughest team. The 35 points were the most Minnesota (7-3) had allowed all season; its one sack tied for its fewest; its zero takeaways are the fewest. No other offense had enjoyed such success against them to this point, not even Detroit, Green Bay and Chicago, the NFC North rivals who also boast explosive offenses. The performance was so one-sided that 49ers coach and offensive play caller Kyle Shanahan was asked whether this is the best team he has led in his 10 seasons in San Francisco. “No, but it’s still early,” Shanahan said. “We got to earn that and we’re halfway through the year. We’ve done some good things but it’s still to be determined. (A season) is 7 months long. We know how we’ve been so far but we’re halfway there and we got a long way to go.” The mood was also light enough that tight end George Kittle, after catching two touchdowns, wore a lucha libre mask to his postgame press availability. “Did I distract you at all?” Kittle said to his teammate on the dais. Quarterback Brock Purdy shook his head. Little distracted Purdy while completing 21 of his 26 passes for 255 yards and three touchdowns and taking away Minnesota’s greatest strength — its ability to speed up quarterbacks by sending waves of pressure. Rather than be rattled, Purdy completed his first eight passes against Vikings blitzes for two touchdowns. When one rushing defender leaped to hit Purdy or at least deflect his pass, the quarterback calmly pump-faked, dipped down and found a receiver for a 7-yard gain instead of 7-yard loss. On another play, he leaped into the air behind his blockers before firing an accurate strike. “We never recommend the jump pass,” Shanahan said. “But when he pulls it off and it works, then we congratulate him.” The scariest thing for the rest of the NFL is that if Purdy could play cool and collected against pressure like that, the rest of his opponents will be tame by comparison. Indeed, all season, Purdy ranks first among all quarterbacks in both yards per attempt and passing touchdowns when facing a blitz, per ESPN. “Best player in the game right now,” 49ers receiver Mike Evans said. “He’s super dialed-in. The way he prepares, the way he competes, he’s tough. I always thought he was underrated.” No receiver was targeted more than seven times, but the mixture of passes, runs and misdirections by Shanahan kept the Vikings from keying onto any of the nine players who caught a pass Sunday. Purdy’s passer rating wasn’t only the highest allowed by the Vikings this season — it was also the highest QBR allowed by Minnesota in the regular season since ESPN began tracking the statistic 20 years ago. Entering the week, the matchup between Shanahan and Flores was more than simply an exceptional appetizer to the league’s slate of Thanksgiving week matchups. It was no exaggeration to describe the showdown of the NFL’s most-disruptive defense and its second-highest-scoring offense as one that might be repeated in two months’ time during the NFC Championship. In each of three previous matchups between a Flores defense and Shanahan offense, Flores had won the game while allowing just 17 points. On Sunday, that script flipped. By late in the second quarter, the 49ers’ offense had already scored 21 points. San Francisco widened its lead further, to 28-10, when Ji’Ayir Brown intercepted Minnesota’s Kirk Cousins and ran it back for a touchdown. It wasn’t even halftime and the Vikings had already allowed more points, and trailed by more points, than they had all season. “Our game plan was so good,” Kittle told ESPN. “It was really just trying to take advantage of how much they pressure us. Try to get guys in those little gaps. ... And then, when you look out there and you see Mike Evans, Keenan Allen, Christian McCaffery, Deebo Samuel, it really makes my heart happy.” When Vikings star receiver Justin Jefferson fumbled on the opening drive of the second half, the game was effectively over and so was any doubt about the best team, so far, in the NFC. That wasn’t solely because of their offensive performance, either. After allowing 40 points last week against Dallas, the 49ers’ defense forced two turnovers, including the pick-six, and held Minnesota to 1-of-3 on fourth-down attempts. The Vikings had allowed opponents to travel an average of just 25.2 yards per drive this season, second-fewest in the league. And those drives turned into scores just 26% of the time, a league-best rate. San Francisco, though, found little resistance. Its first three touchdown drives traveled 72, 67 and 65 yards, respectively. Its final scoring drive, in the fourth quarter, chewed up 7 minutes of time while traveling 98 yards. It was 4-for-4 scoring once inside the red zone. It was tempting to pin the performance on their preparation, after spending several days last week practicing at the Air Force Academy in Colorado Springs, Colorado, to acclimate to Mexico City’s elevation. But San Francisco has looked like a team to beat since Week 1, too, when it convincingly took out the Super Bowl contender Los Angeles Rams in Australia. San Francisco’s control was so secure that it removed Purdy and played backup quarterback Mac Jones with 5 minutes still to play in the fourth quarter. “I think their quarterback’s really good,” Vikings coach Kevin O’Connell, a former NFL quarterback himself, said. “And I think they got a bunch of really good players.”

articles.title: San Francisco 49ers 35-10 Minnesota Vikings: Brock Purdy dismantles Vikings defence with three touchdown passes
articles.summary: Brock Purdy starred as San Francisco 49ers extended their season record to 9-1 with a 35-10 win against Minnesota Vikings in Mexico City; Purdy threw three touchdown passes and gained 255 yards; watch the 2026 NFL season live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
Played in front of a raucous, pro-49ers crowd at Estadio Azteca, the game had been billed as a heavyweight showdown between one of the NFL's most dangerous offences, San Francisco (9ǃ), and a Minnesota Vikings (7ǅ) defence that had unsettled quarterbacks throughout the season with its aggressive blitz-heavy approach.

However, Purdy proved more than equal to the challenge, delivering an imperious performance and carving up the Minnesota defence with three touchdown passes in the first half alone.

"You have to be aggressive and don't second-guess yourself," Purdy said.

"Obviously, try to read it the best you can, but when you have players that can go get the ball, allow them to go and make plays.

"I feel like our guys did that around me today. It wasn't a one-man show. It was a really good team effort."

Coordinator Brian Flores' schemes didn't work at all against the 49ers quarterback, who orchestrated three touchdown drives on the Niners' first four possessions.

"He was so good. He was quick, he was confident, he threw strikes," said tight end George Kittle, who caught two TD passes.

"He's playing with confidence, he understands the offense, he is confident in the offense. He knows the offense. When he goes out there he has this aura in the huddle."

San Francisco headed into half-time with a commanding 28-10 lead, fuelled by Purdy's outstanding performance and a pick-six from Ji'Ayir Brown, who intercepted Kirk Cousins and returned it for a touchdown.

The 49ers set the tone from the outset, marching downfield on an impressive seven-play, 72-yard opening drive. Purdy completed all four of his passes for 55 yards, capping the possession with a 17-yard touchdown pass to George Kittle.

After being forced to punt on their second possession, San Francisco quickly regained momentum, with Purdy orchestrating touchdown drives on each of their next two possessions.

He threw an eight-yard touchdown pass to Kittle to make it 14ǉ before connecting with Mike Evans for a four-yard score to extend the lead to 21.

Brown then intercepted Cousins on the Vikings' next play from scrimmage and returned it 18 yards for a touchdown, further extending San Francisco's advantage.

The 49ers continued to impress after the break, producing a superb 98-yard touchdown drive that featured chants of "MVP!" for Purdy. The possession was capped off by Christian McCaffrey's six-yard touchdown run, effectively putting the game beyond doubt early in the fourth quarter.

Purdy finished 21 of 26 for 255 yards and a remarkable passer rating of 146, more than double the league-low 69.5 rating Minnesota's defence had allowed opponents entering the game.

Reflecting on his quarterback's performance, 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan said: "Seemed like he played a lot better than a lot of other guys have versus them, because not many people play that good versus that defence.

"There's a reason for that. It's a huge challenge. It was hard looking at it all week. Brock didn't get rattled, which he really never does. I think it says a lot about Brock."

However, the emphatic victory was overshadowed by a serious injury to right tackle Colton McKivitz, who broke and dislocated his left ankle during the second quarter.

McKivitz was injured at the end of a four-yard run by McCaffrey, after being caught in a collision with opposing players. The severity of the injury was immediately apparent, with team-mates visibly distressed as medical staff rushed onto the field. Left tackle Trent Williams slammed his helmet to the ground, while several 49ers players took a knee as McKivitz received treatment.

Head coach Shanahan later confirmed that the injury was similar to the one that brought linebacker Fred Warner's season to an end last October.

"That was really crushing," Shanahan said. "Colton has had an unbelievable year. It was tough to see him go down like that."

Despite the convincing victory, McKivitz's injury provided a sobering moment for San Francisco, with the team now facing the prospect of being without a key member of its offensive line.

It's the Vikings' second defeat in three weeks, with Cousins also throwing a pick-six in Week Nine for the Las Vegas Raiders, before he was traded back to Minnesota.

He became the first player ever to throw a pick-six for two teams against the same opponent in a season.

Cousins went 26 for 38 for 235 yards and was unable to follow up his winning performance last week at Green Bay.

"There's no group that I have more confidence in than not only those players on defense and that coaching staff." Vikings coach Kevin O'Connell said.

"There's just no really other way to put it. We just got beat tonight.

"They made some plays. I think the quarterback [Purdy] is really good and they got a bunch of really good players and they execute at a really high level."

The 49ers will look to extend their 9-1 record as they welcome Seattle Seahawks on Sunday, while the Vikings face off against the Atlanta Falcons in Minneapolis on the same night.

articles.title: NFL results: San Francisco 49ers, Buffalo Bills and Kansas City Chiefs win in week 11
articles.summary: The San Francisco 49ers and Buffalo Bills remain the pacesetters in each conference of the NFL.
articles.body:
The San Francisco 49ers and Buffalo Bills remain the pacesetters in each conference of the NFL after both won again.

The 49ers beat the Minnesota Vikings in the last of a record nine international games this season to take their record to 9-1.

They lead the way in the NFC, with the Chicago Bears and their divisional rivals the Detroit Lions next best on 8-2.

Buffalo improved to 9-1 for the first time since 1991 and lead the AFC from another pair of divisional rivals, with the Kansas City Chiefs and Denver Broncos on 8-2.

The Chiefs and Broncos could be joined by the Cincinnati Bengals, who conclude week 11 at the Washington Commanders on Monday.

Mexico hosted the first regular-season game to be played outside the US in October 2005, and the NFL returned to the country on Sunday following a four-year absence.

After being redeveloped for the 2026 World Cup, the Azteca Stadium staged its sixth NFL game and the third involving San Francisco, who kicked off this season's international series by beating the Los Angeles Rams in Australia in week one.

Sunday's game pitted the league's best offence against the best defence and was the first international game to be played in the primetime slot.

The Vikings defence had not conceded more than 23 points in a game this season, but the 49ers offence outsmarted them in front of 85,612 fans in Mexico City.

The 49ers scored four touchdowns in the first half - two by George Kittle - before running out 35-10 winners.

Mike Evans returned after missing three games with an Achilles problem to finish with 109 receiving yards and a touchdown.

With the game played at high altitude - about 7,220ft (2,240m) above sea level - some players used oxygen masks on the sidelines.

San Francisco face another test of their Super Bowl credentials next Sunday at home to the defending champions, the 6-4 Seattle Seahawks, who were one of six teams on their bye this week.

The Jacksonville Jaguars entered week 11 with the best regular-season record over the past 12 months - they had lost only twice - and had scored more than 30 points in each of their past four games.

Yet the New York Giants managed to stifle the Jaguars for three quarters and led 20-6 heading into what proved to be a dramatic final quarter.

The Jaguars had to settle for a field goal after a controversial call denied them a touchdown, but they still threatened a fightback as they cut the deficit to five.

The Giants offence did enough to stop the Jags getting one more possession, though, and secure a 23-18 home win.

It was the first time the NFC East leaders have beaten a team with a winning record this season and they are now 6-3-1, while the 7-3 Jags remain in charge of the AFC South.

In his first season as head coach, John Harbaugh could lead the Giants to their first division title since 2011, when 'Big Blue' went on to claim their fourth Super Bowl.

They remain clear of the 5-6 Dallas Cowboys, whose rollercoaster season continued with a 51-30 win over the Tennessee Titans, with Dak Prescott throwing for 325 yards and four touchdowns.

Kelce at the double before tough Chiefs run

Although Josh Allen threw for more interceptions than touchdowns (2-1), the Bills were still comfortable, beating the Miami Dolphins 26-9 for their sixth straight victory.

The Bills have a mouth-watering Thanksgiving clash on Thursday (01:20 GMT, Friday) at home to the Kansas City Chiefs, who beat the Arizona Cardinals 34-7.

Travis Kelce had two scores for the Chiefs, claiming multiple touchdowns in the same game for the first time since a play-off win over Buffalo in January 2024.

Emmett Johnson registered a combined 143 yards and a touchdown in the absence of fellow running back Kenneth Walker, who is set to return from a minor groin problem against Buffalo.

That game kicks off a crucial five-game stretch for Kansas City, which continues against the Rams, the Bengals, the Patriots and the 49ers.

The Chiefs are joint top of the AFC West with the Denver Broncos, who kept the pressure on by beating the Las Vegas Raiders 38-24 for a sixth straight win.

Fernando Mendoza, this year's first overall draft pick, threw his first three touchdown passes but then a pick-six which allowed Denver to clinch victory, after Jonah Coleman had run in three scores for the Broncos.

Bears and Lions set up Thanksgiving showdown

The home team won all seven of the early games, and they were favourites heading into all but one of those match-ups.

The only underdogs to emerge victorious were the Philadelphia Eagles (3-7), who beat the Pittsburgh Steelers 19-16 to end a seven-game losing streak.

The Bears and Lions both won to remain joint-top of the NFC North, and they have a Thanksgiving showdown in Detroit on Thursday (18:00 GMT).

The Bears beat the New Orleans Saints 21-13, with Chicago's Jeffery Simmons claiming three sacks, taking his tally to five in three games since his blockbuster trade from Tennessee.

On Thursday he will try to stop this season's rushing leader Jahmyr Gibbs, who rushed for another 98 yards and two touchdowns in Detroit's 31-21 win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

The NFL's highest-paid running back has now tied Barry Sanders for the most rushing touchdowns (52) before turning 25 – and Gibbs' birthday is not until March.
