articles.title: NFL Week 11: A Travis Kelce game years in the making, and Dak Prescott keeps dealing
articles.summary: Week 11 of the NFL season featured a throwback performance by Travis Kelce, a nail-biter in New York, and the second start for Raiders rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza.
articles.body: Week 11 of the NFL season featured a throwback performance by Travis Kelce, a nail-biter in New York, and the second start for Raiders rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza. Here’s everything you need to know from Sunday. A vintage day for Mahomes and Kelce The Kansas City Chiefs rolled over the Arizona Cardinals, cruising to a 34-7 victory. Tight end Travis Kelce caught two touchdowns — his first regular season game with at least two receiving scores since 2022. Kelce hasn’t caught more than five touchdowns in a season since 2022, and he’s now up to four this year with seven games to go. Patrick Mahomes is also on a tear. After a three-touchdown performance against the Cardinals, Mahomes has thrown for 13 scores with zero interceptions over the last four games, during which Kansas City has a 3-1 record. It should be another classic on Thanksgiving when Mahomes, Kelce and the Chiefs take on Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills, who beat the Miami Dolphins 26-9 on Sunday. The Giants keep finding a way New York improved to 6-3-1 after holding on for a 23-18 win over the Jacksonville Jaguars. That’s the best win for head coach John Harbaugh in his first season with the Giants, taking down a team that was 16-3 in its last 19 regular season games. There was controversy late, as what appeared to be a touchdown catch by Jaguars receiver Parker Washington was instead ruled incomplete. Jacksonville also opted for a field goal from inside the 10 while trailing 23-15 with under four minutes to go. The Jags never saw the ball again. New York was outgained on offense, but its defense forced two turnovers to overcome an anemic passing attack. The Giants remained in the driver’s seat to win the NFC East. Eagles get their first win since September It’s been a long fall for Philadelphia, which went two whole months between wins before a 19-16 victory over their cross-state rival Pittsburgh Steelers in Week 11. Eagles quarterback Joe Milton did just enough for the win, ending their seven-game losing streak. Aaron Rodgers, meanwhile, struggled again. Rodgers averaged only 5.2 yards per attempt, and was sacked five times in the loss. The Steelers have now dropped two straight after a four-game win streak. Rodgers has avoided big mistakes, but in turn has failed to consistently make big plays. His current average yards per passing attempt is a career-low mark. More heartbreak for the Ravens After a 4-1 start, Baltimore has lost six straight games. And for the second straight week, a late turnover ruined a potential comeback. The Ravens played a back-and-forth thriller against the Carolina Panthers on Sunday, ultimately losing 35-33. The game featured five total turnovers (four by Baltimore), a safety, and even a kickoff return for a touchdown. The Panthers took a late lead on a 37-yard field goal with under two minutes to go. Jacoby Brissett, making his second start for the Ravens, had an opportunity to lead a game-winning drive if he could get the offense into field-goal range. But with under 40 seconds to go, Brissett tried to take a shot Rashod Bateman after a long scramble in the backfield, only for his pass to be deflected backward into the arms of a Carolina defender. Here come the Cowboys A week after scoring 40 points in a loss to the San Francisco 49ers, Dallas came back with another offensive explosion in a 51-30 win over the Tennessee Titans. Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott was sensational, posting a season-best 147.3 passer rating in the win. Prescott finished with 325 yards and four touchdowns against the hapless Titans, who fell to 1-9. Prescott has certainly done just about all he can for the Cowboys so far this season. After Sunday’s win, Prescott has thrown for over 3,000 yards with 25 touchdowns and only six interceptions this year. In his last five games, Prescott has 17 total touchdowns and zero interceptions, but Dallas has gone only 3-2 in that stretch. No ‘Mendoza Magic’ Making his second career start, No. 1 overall pick in April’s draft Fernando Mendoza had a chance to lead the Raiders to a game-winning or game-tying score against the Denver Broncos, but instead he threw a game-sealing pick six. Still, Mendoza showed improvement from his first start. He threw for 267 yards and three touchdowns in the 38-24 loss, recording his first career passing touchdown in the process. All were improvements over his first start, though Mendoza’s interception was the first of his career, and he also suffered five sacks. The Lions and Bears keep pace Both Detroit and Chicago won, keeping each side at 8-2 before their massive Turkey Day showdown. The Lions pulled away from the Tampa Bay Buccaneers late, winning 31-21. The Bears, meanwhile, survived a scare from the New Orleans Saints on a rainy day in Chicago, holding on for a 21-13 victory. The race for the No. 1 pick There are three one-win teams left in the NFL after Week 11: the Chargers, Dolphins and Titans. Based on strength of schedule, Tennessee would have the top pick in next year’s draft if the season ended today, followed by Los Angeles and then Miami. The top of the draft order could very well come down to Week 16, when the Chargers and Dolphins are scheduled to face off. 49ers, now 9-1, send a message In the “Sunday Night Football” nightcap, Minnesota kicker Will Reichard’s 71-yard field goal attempt came up just a few feet short from setting a new NFL record. Unfortunately for the Vikings, the rest of the game wasn’t nearly so close. San Francisco improved to 9-1 and made a statement with its 35-10 win over Minnesota (7-3). By only halftime the 49ers had 28 points, more than the Vikings’ havoc-causing defense had allowed in a game all season. CORRECTION (Nov. 23, 2026, 7:24 a.m. ET): A headline and the text in a previous version of this article misstated which NFL division the New York Giants play in. They play in the NFC East, not NFC North.

articles.body: Patrick Mahomes had a brief message for Colton McKivitz after the San Francisco 49ers offensive lineman suffered a frightening leg injury against the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday night. The incident occurred during the second quarter of their NFC showdown in Mexico City, forcing medical staff to rush onto the field. Mahomes, who was watching the game, quickly responded on social media with three words: “Prayers up man.” His reaction also drew appreciation from 49ers fans, despite the history between San Francisco and Kansas City.Patrick Mahomes sends support to Colton McKivitz after frightening injuryMcKivitz's injury came during a play involving running back Christian McCaffrey. As players converged around the ball carrier, several bodies rolled onto the veteran offensive lineman's leg. He immediately needed medical attention, and trainers rushed onto the field to assess the damage.The 49ers medical staff placed McKivitz's leg in an air cast before taking him off the field on a cart. NBC did not show a replay of the incident, but the reaction from players offered a clear indication of how serious the situation appeared.One of the most visible reactions came from Trent Williams. The veteran left tackle slammed his helmet onto the ground in frustration as McKivitz received treatment. For teammates who share the offensive line with him, watching a fellow player suffer such an injury was a difficult sight.Mahomes was among those following the game and did not wait long to express his concern. The Kansas City Chiefs quarterback posted, “Prayers up man.” It was a short message, but it carried a clear show of support for a player facing an uncertain moment.The response also showed how moments of concern can cut across team rivalries. Mahomes and the Chiefs have faced San Francisco in two Super Bowls, but that history did not stop him from acknowledging what McKivitz was going through.49ers fans appreciate Mahomes as McKivitz's injury raises concernMahomes' message received a positive response from San Francisco supporters. Although the 49ers and Chiefs have developed a competitive rivalry through their Super Bowl meetings, fans were quick to appreciate the quarterback's gesture.One fan defended Mahomes against those who regularly criticise him, writing, “People that hate Mahomes are pure idiots. He’s a class act always,”The reaction reflected the respect Mahomes has earned beyond Kansas City. His message did not need a lengthy explanation or a public statement. He simply acknowledged an opposing player who had suffered a frightening injury.For San Francisco, McKivitz's absence could carry significant importance. The 49ers selected him in the fifth round of the 2020 NFL Draft out of West Virginia. He did not immediately become a regular starter, making just five starts across his first three NFL seasons.That changed in 2023, when he secured a more prominent role on the offensive line. Since then, McKivitz has become a dependable presence, starting every game over the past four seasons. Sunday's appearance marked his 61st consecutive start for the franchise.That kind of consistency is valuable for any offensive line, particularly one tasked with protecting the quarterback and creating space for the running game. His injury therefore leaves San Francisco with more than just an immediate concern about one player.The 49ers will now have to assess the extent of the damage and consider how his absence could affect their offensive line. For McKivitz, the immediate priority is recovery. articles.title: NFL Week 11 Sunday takeaways: Brock Purdy is a game manager and an MVP candidate, Aaron Rodgers is cooked
articles.summary: From Brock Purdy beating the Vikings’ blitz to the Cowboys giving up 30 points and still winning by 21, here’s one takeaway from every game on the NFL’s Week 11 Sunday slate.
articles.body: Week 11 didn't look great on paper. When I checked the betting lines on Thursday, five of the 13 games had double-digit spreads. I was hoping some of those matchups would look better on the field. Anyone who watched the early window knows how that worked out. You'd think a guy who spent Thursday writing about how predictable these games looked could at least pick a winner. Six of the seven favorites in the early window won outright. Naturally, I found the seventh and laid the points. CHIEFS AND BILLS TAKE CARE OF BUSINESS AHEAD OF THE NFL’S BIGGEST REGULAR-SEASON GAME Here's my biggest takeaway from each game on the Week 11 Sunday slate. Chiefs 34, Cardinals 7 Takeaway: What did you expect? The Chiefs throttled the hapless Cardinals, as expected. Travis Kelce had a vintage Kelce game, catching six passes for 74 yards and two touchdowns. It seems like the future Hall of Fame tight end is in better shape and more focused on football this season, which is good for Kansas City. Ultimately, this was simply an appetizer for the main course: Kansas City Chiefs at Buffalo Bills on Thanksgiving night. Not only does that game feature two of the best teams in the NFL, but it has massive implications for the race for the No. 1 seed in the AFC. Buckle up. Bills 26, Dolphins 9 Takeaway: What did you expect? This might seem lazy, but... yeah, OK, it's lazy. We're 11 weeks into the season. There's only so much to say about each team. The Bills entered the game as two-touchdown favorites for a reason and coasted to an easy victory, much like the Chiefs. And if you read the Chiefs blurb, you already know where this is going. A win over Kansas City on Thanksgiving night would put the Bills in prime position to do something they've never done in the Josh Allen era: earn the No. 1 seed in the AFC and force their opponents to go through Buffalo. That makes Thursday night's game a huge one for both teams, so buckle up. Wait, that's really lazy. Get your popcorn ready. Did I use that one last week? Whatever. Insert new cliché here. Cowboys 51, Titans 30 Takeaway: The Cowboys aren't very good, but they are fun to watch. Hey, the NFL needs some teams that just decide they don't want to play defense and focus only on scoring as many points as possible. That pretty much sums up the Dallas Cowboys, who have scored 91 points in their past two games... but also allowed 76. The Cowboys are averaging 37.2 points per game over their past five but are just 3-2 in that stretch. Part of that is because they can't stop committing penalties, including 11 more for 128 yards against Tennessee. And part is because the defense stinks. Who cares, though, amirite? Points are points, and good for you if you drafted pieces of the Cowboys offense on your fantasy football team. Panthers 35, Ravens 33 Takeaway: The NFC South has a team at .500! It was basically a perfect day for the Panthers, who not only won to move to 5-5 but also saw the Buccaneers and Saints both lose while the Falcons were on a bye. That gives Carolina a two-game lead in the NFC South, which is pretty insane when you stop and think about it. If the Panthers were in the NFC North, they'd be in last place and three games back of first. But that doesn't really matter, does it? Nope, the Panthers are in pole position to win the NFC South for the second straight year. And it's possible they do it both times without even having a winning record. Bears 21, Saints 13 Takeaway: I want to be sold on the Bears, but I'm just not. And this game didn't help. The Bears raced out to a 16-0 lead midway through the second quarter and really should have cruised to an easy victory at home against a Saints team that entered 3-6. But Chicago allowed New Orleans to get back into the game, thanks in part to a bad Caleb Williams interception. If the Saints hadn't missed a 47-yard field goal, they could have gone into halftime trailing just 16-13 and put even more pressure on Chicago. They didn't, though, and to be fair, it never felt like the Bears were going to lose the game. It just felt like they should have been more dominant at home against a bad team. Eagles 19, Steelers 16 Takeaway: I was right, and I never should have doubted myself. After Pittsburgh's first two games, I declared that Aaron Rodgers was done and this team was dead. Then the 42-year-old went out and had a few good games, and I backtracked like a wuss. But I was right: Rodgers is cooked. The Steelers offense is embarrassingly bad and basically the opposite of the Dallas Cowboys. It is not fun to watch. Like, at all. Pittsburgh didn't score its only touchdown until 1:21 remained against an Eagles team that had lost seven straight. DK METCALF DISQUALIFIED FROM STEELERS GAME FOR UNSPORTSMANLIKE PENALTIES INCLUDING POKING OPPONENT'S FACEMASK The offensive line can't block, Rodgers isn't mobile enough to consistently escape the pressure, and the receivers don't generate any separation from defensive backs. In an AFC that features teams like the Bengals, Chiefs and Bills, the Steelers aren't a serious threat to make a run. They should start thinking about what the future looks like after Rodgers. Lions 31, Buccaneers 21 Takeaway: That's more like it. The usually explosive Lions offense was pretty tame for a stretch, failing to score more than 20 points in three straight games (but still going 3-0 against the Packers, Vikings and Dolphins). They've come to life over the past two weeks, though, dropping 66 points and showing that it's hard to hold down an offense that features Jahmyr Gibbs, Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jameson Williams. Speaking of Gibbs, he deserves some serious MVP consideration. He'll never win because it's a QB award, but I'm not sure any skill player is more important to his team than Gibbs is to the 8-2 Lions. He didn't even have one of his best games against Tampa Bay and still went for 118 yards from scrimmage and two touchdowns. The Offensive Player of the Year race is going to be a fun one to watch because Gibbs, Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Ja'Marr Chase all have a pretty good case this season. Jets 27, Chargers 24 Takeaway: Can’t blame the schedule for this one. Look, the Chargers are terrible. But to be fair, the early-season schedule didn’t do them any favors. Five of their eight losses before Sunday came against teams that currently have winning records, and those five came in a row against the Bills, Seahawks, Broncos, Chiefs and Rams. Losing at home to a two-win Jets team that hadn’t scored a touchdown in either of its past two games? That one’s on the Chargers. Now, if you’re a Chargers fan, this might actually be good news. Los Angeles is right there with the one-win Dolphins and Titans in the race for the No. 1 pick in the 2027 NFL Draft. And guess where the Chargers go in Week 16? Miami. Good luck convincing either fan base to root for a win in that one. Broncos 38, Raiders 24 Takeaway: If you think I’m going to give Sean Payton credit, you clearly don’t know anything about me. No, I don’t suddenly believe in Sean Payton, Bo Nix or the rest of the Broncos. Denver has two good wins this season, against the Rams and Chiefs. Both came at home, and both took a controversial call going Denver’s way. Now I’m supposed to change my mind because they beat the Raiders at home, too? With Fernando Mendoza making his second NFL start? Please. At 8-2, the Broncos are going to give the Monday morning sports shows an excuse to put them in the same conversation as the Chiefs, Bills and Bengals. Don’t buy it. Denver is an above-average team with the most overrated head coach in the NFL. Give the Broncos a favorable matchup and I can see them winning a wild-card game. That’s about as much credit as you’re getting out of me. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE Giants 23, Jaguars 18 Takeaway: I tried to warn y’all about the Jaguars. Look, I get it. People are tired of seeing the Chiefs, Bills and Bengals play for the AFC championship. I understand wanting the Jags to be the team that breaks through and makes a Cinderella run. I just don’t see it. Trevor Lawrence piled up some yards late, but he threw two picks and easily could’ve thrown a couple more. And the Giants gave Jacksonville every chance to come back. But afterward, on social media, the player ruined his own moment. No question. And he used the same words the terrorists' leader instructed his henchmen to utter repeatedly as their plot unfolded and some piloted two planes into the sides of the Twin Towers in lower Manhattan. Carter's performance sent the NFL a message that he's improving, developing, coming into his own. But then Carter went on social media and sent a different message. Whatever Allahu Akbar's solemn religious meaning, the fact is that in the aftermath of the Sept. 11 attacks, the FBI recovered a four-page handwritten document in Arabic found in the luggage of terrorist ringleader Mohamed Atta. Written as a tactical manual for the hijackers, the letter explicitly instructed them on how to use the phrase "Allahu Akbar" at key stages of the operation. articles.body: Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers did not hide his frustration after Sunday's 19-16 defeat to the Philadelphia Eagles, but his postgame comments went beyond the result. Rodgers questioned the offense's heavy reliance on the passing game and made it clear that Pittsburgh needs to get back to running the football. He also addressed DK Metcalf's ejection, although he was far less willing to discuss his teammate's actions. With the Steelers now 6-4, Rodgers knows another missed opportunity could hurt their playoff position.Aaron Rodgers wants the Steelers to rely more on the running gameThe Steelers struggled to find their rhythm against Philadelphia, going without a touchdown through the first three quarters. Max Hurleman's fourth-quarter score gave Pittsburgh some life, but it came too late to prevent a defeat that ended the Eagles' seven-game losing streak.For Aaron Rodgers, the problem was not simply the final score. He was unhappy with how the offense developed and felt Pittsburgh had moved too far away from its running game. The veteran quarterback does not want the Steelers to depend on his arm for most of their production.“Run the ball. Yeah, we like to run the ball. That makes everything easier.“We’re not trying to throw the ball 50 times a game.”Rodgers acknowledged that game situations can force an offense to change its approach. However, he believes Pittsburgh's best chance of producing consistent results comes from establishing the run early and making opposing defenses respect it.“Some games might dictate some of that stuff, but we got to run the football and generate explosive runs, and that sets up everything else.”His comments also offered a clear indication of where he believes the Steelers need to improve. A stronger ground attack would take some pressure off Rodgers while giving the offense more options in crucial situations.Aaron Rodgers keeps his message to DK Metcalf privateRodgers was also asked about DK Metcalf's ejection during the defeat. The wide receiver's departure added another problem to an already frustrating afternoon for Pittsburgh, but Rodgers chose his words carefully when discussing the incident.He did not defend what happened, although he made it clear that he was not interested in discussing the details publicly."That was disappointing," Rodgers told reporters. "Obviously, we love DK. And I don't know what was going on out there, what was happening. But, yeah, we can't have two of those."When reporters asked what message he had for Metcalf, Rodgers refused to share their conversation."I'm not going to tell you that," Rodgers said. "I'm going to talk to DK. We're real good friends, so."The response suggested that Aaron Rodgers would rather handle the matter directly with his teammate than turn it into another public discussion. He has been willing to speak openly about the Steelers' shortcomings, but this was a conversation he wanted to keep between them.There is also little doubt that Metcalf's absence created another issue for an offense already struggling to produce. articles.title: Travis Kelce gives Chiefs fans a reason to wonder about his future after breaking Rob Gronkowski's record
articles.summary: Travis Kelce gave Kansas City Chiefs fans another reason to think about his future after delivering a record-breaking performance against the Arizona
articles.body: Travis Kelce gave Kansas City Chiefs fans another reason to think about his future after delivering a record-breaking performance against the Arizona Cardinals. The 37-year-old tight end scored twice in Sunday's 34-7 win, moving past Rob Gronkowski on the NFL's all-time touchdown list for tight ends. But it was his response to a question about playing his 100th regular-season game at Arrowhead Stadium that caught attention. Asked about reaching the milestone, Kelce offered a short answer that sounded more like a promise than a farewell. "Cheers to 100 more," he said.Travis Kelce moves past Rob Gronkowski with two touchdownsKelce made sure his milestone night counted on the field. His first touchdown came on an 8-yard pass from Patrick Mahomes in the opening quarter. It was his 109th career touchdown, including the playoffs, taking him past Gronkowski into third place among tight ends in NFL history.He added another score in the second quarter, catching a 22-yard touchdown pass to reach 110. That leaves him within reach of two more legendary names. Antonio Gates leads the list with 118 touchdowns, while Tony Gonzalez sits second with 115.The performance also carried some personal significance. Kelce played his 100th regular-season game at Arrowhead, becoming only the fourth player in Chiefs franchise history to reach that mark. He also recorded his first multi-touchdown game in nearly four years.And he did it while dealing with an ankle problem. Chiefs head coach Andy Reid confirmed earlier in the week that Kelce had a high-ankle sprain, an injury he has dealt with before. Despite that concern, the veteran tight end remained a major part of Kansas City's offense.Kelce also joined a rare group of NFL players by scoring at least twice from scrimmage in one half at age 37 or older. Only four players have managed that feat, including Hall of Fame wide receiver Jerry Rice.Former NFL safety Ryan Clark was impressed with what he saw, particularly given Kelce's age and the comparisons he continues to face."Travis Kelce is still doing it at a high level for the tight end position. He'll be compared to the younger guys and his younger self, but man, he's getting the job done this year for his team."Kelce's latest achievement adds to an already remarkable season. Earlier, he and Mahomes passed Gates and Philip Rivers for the most passing yards by a tight end-quarterback combination in NFL history. Kelce has also broken the NFL record for career yards after the catch.Travis Kelce's latest comments bring retirement questions backThe bigger talking point, however, remains how much longer Kelce intends to play. Retirement discussions have followed him since Kansas City's Super Bowl loss in February 2025. He seriously considered ending his career after that season before deciding to return for a 14th year.Chiefs general manager Brett Veach previously revealed that Kelce made his intentions clear shortly after the team's final game of 2025. He walked into Veach's office less than 24 hours after the loss and delivered a message that left little room for doubt."I'm not going out like this."Kelce has also spoken openly about his desire to keep playing. During an earlier conversation with ESPN's Chris Berman, he explained that football still holds his attention and that he is not ready to move on to life after the NFL."I love this game so much that I'm not ready to go into that next phase yet."His latest "Cheers to 100 more" comment fits that mindset, although it does not necessarily confirm how many seasons he has left. At 37, every strong performance naturally brings fresh questions about his future. Yet Kelce continues to produce at a level few tight ends can match.Kansas City improved to 8-2 with its third consecutive victory. Mahomes completed 27 of 39 passes for 324 yards and three touchdowns, while Emmett Johnson rushed for 105 yards and a score on 23 carries. The Cardinals, who were without rookie quarterback Carson Beck because of back spasms, managed just seven points.Kelce has spent his entire NFL career in Kansas City after the Chiefs selected him in the third round of the 2013 draft out of Cincinnati. With Gates and Gonzalez still ahead of him, he has more records to chase. His latest performance suggests he is not ready to stop chasing them.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Colton McKivitz Suffers Gruesome Leg Injury, Latest on 49ers OL After Being Carted Off vs. Vikings
articles.summary: San Francisco 49ers right tackle Colton McKivitz suffered a gruesome leg injury that will likely keep him out for the rest of the season after he was carted off the field against the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday.
articles.body:
San Francisco 49ers right tackle Colton McKivitz suffered a gruesome leg injury that will likely keep him out for the rest of the season after he was carted off the field against the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday.

"It's brutal," 49ers running back Christian McCaffrey said, per ESPN's Nick Wagoner . "He's somebody that is one of the heart and souls of this team, a guy who shows up every day with the right attitude. He's the standard, and we're going to really miss him. We all love him. We're praying for him. It's one of the worst parts about this game is stuff like that, but we love him and we're going to play for him from here on out."

Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes sent his well wishes upon seeing the injury.

The injury comes amid what has been a career year for McKivitz, who has the second-best PFF run block grade among tackles and the seventh-best overall grade among tackles.

McKivitz has been a starter on the Niners' offensive line and has played all 17 games of the season since 2023. He has yet to miss a game this season, though that streak will surely come to an end.

While McKivitz has established himself as a starter, the 30-year-old has had a long road to get to that point. He was a fifth-round draft pick in 2020 and started a handful of games as a rookie, but was waived ahead of the 2021 season, and had to work his way back onto the active roster via the practice squad.

Eventually, he earned the job as a full-time starter ahead of the 2023 campaign, and he's stayed there ever since. He signed a three-year, $45 million deal this offseason despite perhaps being able to earn more elsewhere.

"I want to be on that 10-year wall," McKivitz said after signing that deal. "I don't want to leave here. Obviously being cut, I've got some scars there. But, there was a reason why I was drafted here, why I was cut here, and why I still play here. Now I've had three good seasons of starting and I'm going into the fourth."

Clearly, McKivitz is well loved and well respected by his teammates, which explains the emotional reaction from them after the injury.

articles.body:
New England Patriots coach Mike Vrabel denied being "warned" about a potential degenerative knee issue for star wide receiver A.J. Brown when they worked together on the Tennessee Titans.

Vrabel said Monday on WEEI's The Greg Hill Show (via Mike Reiss of ESPN) the Titans traded Brown in 2022 largely because of financial reasons. The coach cited how much success the three-time Pro Bowler subsequently enjoyed with the Philadelphia Eagles:

Nashville-based radio host Jared Stillman reported earlier this month the Titans' medical staff flagged a possible knee issue for Brown that would become a bigger problem in a few years. Vrabel was purportedly presented with this information "and did not object" to the trade:

Brown averaged 81.2 yards per game and made 62 appearances during his four seasons in Philly. For the most part, he was healthy and productive.

But Patriots lead executive Eliot Wolf confirmed to Yahoo Sports' Jori Epstein in June the organization was aware of a "degenerative knee condition" with the decorated pass-catcher. That obviously wasn't enough to scare New England away from acquiring him.

Vrabel also pushed back on the significance of that revelation.

"I think a lot of things get fabricated, and people tell stories," he told reporters in July. "... We're very confident in where he's at physically."

People are naturally circling back with Brown limited to four games so far in 2026. He has experienced hamstring and knee trouble.

Perhaps it's a little too simplistic to suggest the fears the Titans had four years ago have finally materialized. When he has suited up for the Pats, Brown has looked straightforwardly bad compared to his Eagles peak. That can't be chalked up purely to a knee injury, nor was it something you could've forecasted based on his past performance.

Regardless, New England now finds itself in a terrible spot. The team's big offseason addition isn't having his intended impact, and influential figures such as Vrabel have to allay concerns that Brown is totally cooked.

The 29-year-old is under contract with the Patriots through the 2029 season.

What was supposed to be a marquee match-up between two of the top teams in the NFC on Sunday Night Football was, instead, a one-sided beatdown that reaffirmed that the San Francisco 49ers are the Super Bowl favorites.

articles.title: Lions HC Campbell Reacts to Jameson Williams' Front Flip Celebration After Aidan Hutchinson's Injury
articles.summary: After Detroit Lions star edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson suffered a season-ending torn ACL while celebrating a sack, head coach Dan Campbell is understandably wary of other in-game celebrations.
articles.body:
After Detroit Lions star edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson suffered a season-ending torn ACL while celebrating a sack, head coach Dan Campbell is understandably wary of other in-game celebrations.

So when star receiver Jameson Williams celebrated his 57-yard touchdown reception in Sunday's 31-21 win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers by doing a front flip into the end zone, Campbell couldn't help but feel a rush of nerves.

"He wants your heart to stop," Campbell jokingly told The Athletic's Michael Silver via text.

Skattebo Explains Backflip Despite Plans to Stop

Williams indicated that he doesn't intend to stop his touchdown celebrations, telling ESPN's Lindsey Thiry that he hopes to stick the landing the next time he scores.

"I tried to land it. I didn't really know what to do, so I just did a front flip. I'm gonna try to land one later in the year for y'all, for sure," he said.

Despite Campbell's internal struggle while watching Williams launch himself into the end zone, he didn't change his demeanor for his players. Silver noted that Campbell "was barely fazed, as is his custom." He also called the 50-year-old "a strong, steadying presence" for Detroit in the wake of devastating injuries to Hutchinson and linebacker Jack Campbell (neck).

Even without two of their best defensive players, the Lions extended their streak of holding opponents to 275 or fewer total yards to four straight games. After improving to 8-2, Detroit has firmly established itself as one of the top contenders in the NFC.

"That's been the biggest growth for us," Campbell said after the game , referring to the team's defensive consistency. "The improvement we've had in that group even after losing guys, that's the sign of a championship team."

The Lions will try to earn their seventh straight win when they face the NFC North rival Chicago Bears (8-2) on Thanksgiving Day.

articles.title: David Bailey is first player with 9.5 sacks, six forced fumbles in first 10 NFL games
articles.summary: The Jets haven't won a lot of games this season, but they picked a winner when they drafted linebacker David Bailey with the No. 2 pick in this year's draft.
articles.body:
The Jets haven't won a lot of games this season, but they picked a winner when they drafted linebacker David Bailey with the No. 2 pick in this year's draft.

Bailey had two sacks of Justin Herbert in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Chargers and he forced a fumble on one of those takedowns. That moved Bailey up to 9.5 sacks and six forced fumbles on the season, which makes him the first player to notch those numbers in the first 10 games of his career — Bailey missed one game due to injury — since sacks became an official stat in 1982.

"I'm not surprised and you guys ask me that all the time and I'm going to keep telling you the same thing. We expect that from him," head coach Aaron Glenn said, via a transcript from the team. "I think he's close to 10 sacks right now. The thing that's really sticking out to me is the fact that he's doing everything he can to get the ball back to the offense. He has maybe six or seven forced fumbles this year. I don't know where that is as far as record, but it has to be somewhere up there. Listen, any time he's on the field he gives us a chance for something big to happen. He's a big-time playmaker. I call guys like him 'pressure players.' He's able to make big plays at a time of need and he does a good job at that."

Bailey is now the betting favorite to be the league's defensive rookie of the year and he provides reason for optimism about the future amid another rough season for the Jets.

articles.title: Jets Forced to Make Decision on WR After Career Day vs. Chargers
articles.summary: The New York Jets will be forced to make a move with a WR Safter his career days versus the Los Angeles Chargers. The post Jets Forced to Make Decision on WR...
articles.body:
33-year-old Sterling Shepard just had a career day for the New York Jets during a Week 11 win over the Los Angeles Chargers.

"Sterling Shepard has not had multiple receiving TDs in a season since 2020. He has never had multiple receiving TDs in a single game. Until today. Shepard has now hauled in two TDs from Geno Smith," NFL Insider Jonathan Jones of The Athletic shared.

If they want to keep this talented football player around, the Jets will have to sign him to the active roster. Each player on the practice squad is allowed a maximum of three practice squad elevations per season. Sunday's contest against Los Angeles was Shepard's third elevation. So they will be forced to make a move this week.

"Sterling Shepard has two receiving touchdowns today, the first two-touchdown game of his career. Before today, he last scored a touchdown in November 2023!" the NFL on FOX account shared.

"NFL HISTORY! At 33 years old, Sterling Shepard becomes the OLDEST player in NFL history to record his FIRST career 2-receiving-TD game! The 11-year veteran accomplishes the feat after being elevated from the Jets' practice squad!" Novig posted .

Complains Rain in After Jets Game About Shepard

What a beautiful moment, right? Shepard, who has played for three different teams over the last calendar year, delivers in the red zone for the green and white. Who possibly couldn't be on board with that? Apparently, a lot of people.

"Glad 33 year old Sterling Shepard is helping the Jets win a game that is only going to do way more harm than good. This franchise will never get it. Embarrassing," ESPN New York's Jake Asman reacted on social media.

"nothing quite like Sterling Shepard TDs in late November to tank draft position, no team does it like the Jets man," The Jet Press account posted.

Then they followed it up with this tweet a short while later: "nothing quite like TWO Sterling Shepard TDs in late November to tank draft position."

"The Jets sure know how to pull off a franchise-crushing win at SoFi Stadium late in the season! Sterling Shepard is 2026's Frank Gore," WFAN producer/host Michael Fliegelman wrote.

Do you guys hear how ridiculous that sounds? Okay, so I'm Geno Smith. I'm dropping back to pass oh wow, Shepard is wide open, but damn, I can't throw it to him because the fan base is going to be upset because he doesn't have a long-term future with the team, so they will complain about him getting targets. Maybe someone else is open that the fan base would be more satisfied with if they catch the ball?

Players play. Teams play. Fans want to tank, but the teams do not and will not. You set yourselves up for failure rooting this way. The Jets entered the day 2-8. Fans wanted them to finish 2-15 to secure the best draft position possible. Was that ever likely to happen? No, of course not.

Three losses this season for the Jets have been by multiple scores. Every other game has been a one-score contest. What does that mean? Eventually, if you stay competitive in games long enough, the oblong-shaped football will eventually bounce in your direction.

articles.title: Washington Commanders vs Cincinnati Bengals Week 11: Five Questions with Cincy Jungle
articles.summary: Can the Commanders’ newfound pass defense slow down the NFL’s best passing offense?
articles.body:
It's week 11 of the NFL season and the 3-5-1 Washington Commanders will be facing a 7-2 Cincinnati Bengals team at home at Northwest Stadium in Landover, MD on Monday (today) at 8:15 p.m. ET. The Bengals started the season slow, losing in week 3 to the Steelers and in week 4 to the Jaguars, but have since won 5 straight games including a big division matchup last week against the Steelers that left the Bengals as the leader of the AFC North.

On offense, the Bengals are coached by head coach and playcaller Zac Taylor and offensive coordinator Dan Pitcher. The Bengals have the 6th-ranked offense in the NFL, but it is extremely pass heavy, with the highest pass rate over expectation in the NFL. Thus far, it hasn't been a problem, as the Bengals have the NFL's top-ranked pass offense and 30th-ranked rush offense . This has resulted in the trio of Joe Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase, and Tee Higgins being the most productive QB/pass catcher trio in the NFL since 2006 . The success of the Bengals' offense (and particularly passing game) has also been enabled by the 2nd-best offensive line in the NFL in terms of pressure rate allowed.

On defense, the Bengals are in their second year of DC Al Golden, who was the Bengals' linebackers coach in 2020-2021 before going on to coach defense at Notre Dame and then returning to the Bengals as DC in 2025. Golden runs a pretty simple and coverage-based defense that typically rushes four and leaves a light box (meaning six or fewer defenders in the box). The Bengals actually take this style of defense to an extreme, with the lowest blitz rate in the NFL , the highest rate of light boxes in the NFL, and yet the 3rd-highest rate of man or mixed-man coverage. As a result, the Bengals allow the 2nd-most yards per carry in the NFL, all while allowing the 13th-fewest yards per pass attempt in the NFL.

So why might the Bengals almost dare opponents to run on them? I imagine it has something to do with the fact that teams tend to abandon the run when they are down multiple scores. The Bengals defense really seems to be built around the idea that their offense will be able to establish a lead early and the defense just needs to maintain that lead. As a result, Bengals' opponents pass on them at a 59.6% rate (11th-most in the NFL), despite their glaring weakness being run defense. This could be a good week for Washington to try to establish the run and for Jayden to gain yards on scrambles. This should also be a big week to throw to TEs, as the Bengals are allowing the 3rd-most passing yards to TEs in the NFL (right behind Washington, who are allowing the 2nd-most passing yards to TEs).

I asked Anthony Cosenza of Cincy Jungle five questions to better understand the state of the Bengals and what to look for in this game.

1) The Bengals offense seemed a bit lackluster to start the season, but has really taken off since then. What accounts for their surge in offensive production?

Unfortunately, in the Zac Taylor era, Joe Burrow and Co., have had many years of slow offensive starts. All offseason and into the early portions of the regular season, the Bengals tried to run a lot of under center and "12 personnel" looks, to mixed results, at best, even though they started off 2-0.

Since, the team has transitioned back to their "bread and butter" of shotgun looks and spread their weapons out to create mismatches. To boot, their offensive line has been playing pretty well overall this season. While it hasn't translated to a ton of run game success, they are arguably the best passing offense in the league right now.

2) The Bengals have the 1st-ranked passing offense in the NFL, but the 30th-ranked rushing offense . Why can't they get the run game going and do you think they should try anything different to get it going?

I think it's a myriad of factors. First, I think they've compiled an offensive line that is better built in a spread offense with a high volume of pass attempts. After the Bengals' demolition of the Steelers on Sunday night, tackles Orlando Brown Jr., and Amarius Mims were on the postgame interview, and rhetorically asked about any other tackle tandem in the league that is asked to play the style the Bengals employ.

Secondly, the run game just takes a backseat to how the offense is run. When Joe Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase, and Tee Higgins are playing at a high level, Taylor is going to lean on that trio. Their lack of any notable extensions, free agency additions, and/or trades at the position also points to the run game being a secondary option in this offense.

3) The Bengals defense has transformed from one of the worst in the NFL the last few years to about league average this year. How did they manage that transformation and what's your overall assessment of the defense now?

The short answer is in the additions of Dexter Lawrence II and Jonathan Allen at defensive tackle. Those two have been downright amazing on the field, as well as in the locker room for a group that was both young, and downright lost just a year ago.

But, those two have opened up a number of opportunities for others, too. Boye Mafe has been a great Trey Hendrickson replacement at edge, while the line has allowed their two second-year linebackers (Barrett Carter and Demetrius Knight II) to play a bit more freely. And, while the Bengals have marginally improved in overall run and pass defense statistics, the big key has been their penchant for creating game-swinging plays in the form of both sacks and turnovers.

4) Who is one Bengals player on offense and one on defense that Commanders fans probably don't know much about, but should?

On offense, and for any other team, I'd point out Samaje Perine, who is a personal favorite because of his work ethic, and ability to do all things–especially "the dirty work". But, given his history with Washington, I'll go with Drew Sample, who is a hybrid blend of a blocking tight end, H-Back, fullback, and occasional pass-catcher.

On defense, I think I'll go with either DE Myles Murphy, or DT Kris Jenkins, Jr. Both guys were high picks (Murphy a 2023 first-rounder, and Jenkins at 2024 second-rounder), but they've long been rotational guys buried on the depth chart. While they have also been part of a rotation this year, the duo has combined for 4.5 sacks, and have stepped up at times when others get a little quiet.

5) How should Washington gameplan for this matchup on both sides of the ball?

I think Washington will need to be prepared to score 30-plus points, first and foremost. Unfortunately for the Commanders, they have key players on I.R. for other facets I'd readily point out. Without Terry McLaurin, Stefon Diggs will need to have a big game against an up-and-down Bengals secondary that is seemingly missing Dax Hill this week, while Washington's interior defensive line will want to exploit Dalton Risner's impending absence, even though Javon Kinlaw and Daron Payne are also on I.R. Daniels should also lean on any/all tight ends who can contribute, as that has been an Achilles Heel for the Bengals' defense most of the year.

A companion article to this with my answers to Anthony's questions is linked here .

Thanks again to Anthony Cosenza for taking time out of his day to answer our questions about the Bengals.

articles.title: DK Metcalf Ripped by NFL Coach After Ejection, 'No Moves, Slow Release, Get Jammed and Give Up'
articles.summary: Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver DK Metcalf's ejection from Sunday's 19-16 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles reportedly opened some eyes about his diminishing skills.
articles.body:
Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver DK Metcalf's ejection from Sunday's 19-16 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles reportedly opened some eyes about his diminishing skills.

The Athletic's Mike Sando spoke to a coach who has studied Metcalf, and they ripped the 28-year-old for his lack of production and subpar effort level.

"He has 74 targets and three catching-radius wins," the coach said. "He is poor versus press. I'm talking, stand up, no moves, slow release, get jammed and give up on routes. Then he lacks the route speed to create separation."

Metcalf had just one catch for two yards on four targets before being ejected from Sunday's game due to an altercation with Eagles cornerback Cooper DeJean, which earned him two unsportsmanlike conduct penalties. After the game, Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy called Metcalf's ejection "unacceptable."

A former two-time Pro Bowler, Metcalf was once considered an athletic marvel. However, even with his 6'4", 235-pound frame, Sando noted that he "no longer plays to his size."

"The catching radius part is unbelievable to me where they just don't do that," the coach added. "What else are you going to do with a guy who is not fast enough to separate, lets guys play into his body downfield and doesn't win?"

Through 10 games, Metcalf has 36 catches for 434 yards and two touchdowns. He's reached the 100-yard mark just once this season.

Metcalf will try to bounce back and prove his worth when the Steelers (6-4) face the Denver Broncos (8-2) on Black Friday.

articles.title: Saquon Barkley reveals concerning admission about his health for rest of season
articles.summary: This is not what you want to hear from Saquon.
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Eagles are trying to find consistency as the NFL season enters its final stretch, with every game becoming increasingly important. Injuries have become a growing concern across the league, and players are often forced to balance getting healthy with continuing to compete during a demanding schedule.

Philadelphia is hoping to build momentum after a recent win, but one of its biggest offensive weapons has acknowledged that his health will remain a concern moving forward.

Saquon Barkley admits he won't be 100 percent healthy

Eagles running back Saquon Barkley revealed that he does not expect to be fully healthy for the remainder of the NFL season but intends to continue playing as long as he physically can.

Following Philadelphia's win over the Pittsburgh Steelers on Sunday, Barkley acknowledged that he will likely be dealing with his current ailments for the rest of the season.

Barkley appeared to hurt his shoulder during Sunday's game, although he did not directly address the specific injury when asked about it. Instead, he indicated that his focus would be on rehabilitation and preparing to return for Philadelphia's upcoming game.

"I won't really get into that. I just look forward to rehabbing this week and getting back on Thursday," Barkley said.

Eagles star plans to keep playing despite lingering injuries

Philadelphia has a quick turnaround for its Thanksgiving matchup against the Dallas Cowboys, leaving Barkley with limited time to recover before taking the field again.

The Eagles are coming off a seven-game losing streak and will attempt to build on Sunday's victory. Despite the team's struggles this season, Barkley made it clear that he remains committed to playing through whatever is bothering him.

The opportunity to play on Thanksgiving is also something Barkley clearly values, especially with the Eagles facing Dallas in a nationally televised divisional matchup.

"Playing on Thanksgiving is something we always dream about as kids, against the Dallas Cowboys," Barkley said.

Barkley's admission is concerning for Philadelphia, particularly with several important games remaining on the schedule. However, his willingness to continue playing could provide a boost as the Eagles look to salvage their season and regain some momentum heading into the final weeks.

articles.title: 49ers star Nick Bosa gets booed by fans in Mexico after making harmless comments about cheering
articles.summary: Nick Bosa was showered with boos and Spanish chants at Estadio Azteca after suggesting Mexico City fans needed instructions on when to cheer during games.
articles.body: Nick Bosa's welcome in Mexico was not of the warm variety. Ahead of the showdown between Bosa's San Francisco 49ers and the Minnesota Vikings at Estadio Azteca on Sunday night, the five-time Pro Bowler shared some thoughts about the fan behavior in Mexico City, offering up a suggestion that the crowd in Mexico should be given some instructions on when to cheer during the game. "I think we need some information given to the fans, so they know when to cheer," Bosa said in the lead-up to the game. "Because they just chant the whole time. If we can kind of teach them -- no offense to them and their soccer cheering techniques -- but if they can cheer when we're on defense, that would be great." FRED WARNER CALLS MEXICO CITY NFL GAME 'SUPER SPECIAL' AS MEXICAN ROOTS TAKE CENTER STAGE Bosa's thoughts didn't just come to him out of thin air. He was a member of the 49ers' squad that beat the Arizona Cardinals at Estadio Azteca in 2022, and clearly has memories of the constant chanting throughout the contest, hence the suggestion to the fans. The fans inside the 87,000-seat venue did not take Bosa's comment as a suggestion, however, but instead as an insult. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! When Bosa was shown on the video board inside the stadium during pregame warmups, boos rained down from the crowd. Chants of a Spanish phrase that translates to "a–hole" in English could also be heard throughout the stadium. Bosa's comments were completely innocent, and he even mentioned the very well-known soccer cheering culture typically seen inside the stadium, but one man suggesting to 87,000 paying customers how they should act at a sporting event is never going to sit over well. Bosa and the 49ers went on to trounce the Vikings on Sunday night by a final count of 35-10, with the 29-year-old picking up two quarterback hurries on the final stat sheet. 49ERS' GEORGE KITTLE CHANNELS HIS INNER LUCHADOR AS HE SPORTS WWE STAR'S MASK, PERFORMS CELEBRATION AFTER TD SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER The matchup marked the NFL's first trip to Mexico since the 2022 contest between San Francisco and Arizona. Mexico hosted its first NFL regular-season game in 2005, another matchup between the 49ers and Cardinals, with Arizona earning a 31-14 win at Estadio Azteca.

articles.title: NFL legends react to Panthers S Tre'von Moehrig laying out 320-pound OL
articles.summary: NFL legends Shannon Sharpe and Chad "Ochocinco" Johnson reacted to Panthers S Tre'von Moehrig's booming hit on a 320-pound guard.
articles.body:
Will Lee III wasn't the only Carolina Panthers defensive back to make a splash on Sunday.

Even though his memorable play can't be found in the box score, safety Tre'von Moehrig popped up in yesterday's 35-33 win over the Baltimore Ravens . Watch as the 6-foot-2, 215-pound Moehrig annihilates 6-foot-4, 320-pound guard Olaivavega Ioane on a rush by Ravens running back Justice Hill . . .

Moehrig's booming hit caught the attention of NFL legends Shannon Sharpe and Chad "Ochocinco" Johnson, who talked about the physics of it all on their YouTube show Nightcap . Listen in . . .

Unfortunately for the Panthers defense, this was their worst performance against the run over the past three games. After limiting the Denver Broncos and New Orleans Saints to a combined 2.6 yards per carry between Weeks 9 and 10, they allowed Hill and fellow back Derrick Henry to rush for 163 yards and two touchdowns on just 22 attempts.

Nevertheless, that wasn't enough to push the Ravens past the Panthers—who now hold a two-game lead atop the NFC South.

Along with his blow-up of Ioane, Moehrig finished the victory with a season-high six tackles.

articles.title: Robert Griffin III shares his pick for ‘the best team in the NFL by far’ after Week 11 results
articles.summary: After their dominant win against the Minnesota Vikings, former NFL quarterback Robert Griffin III has picked the San Francisco 49ers as the best team in the...
articles.body:
After their dominant win against the Minnesota Vikings, former NFL quarterback Robert Griffin III has picked the San Francisco 49ers as the best team in the NFL.

Coming into the game with an 8-1 record, the 49ers were expected to face a real challenge against the Vikings, who have the best defence in the league. However, they demolished the defence led by defensive coordinator Brian Flores, with an elite offensive display from their stars.

Brock Purdy threw for 255 yards and had 3 touchdowns throughout the game. Wide receiver Mike Evans, who returned from injury, also showed no signs of rust as he recorded 6 receptions for 109 yards against the Vikings defence.

The defence also did a phenomenal job, shutting down quarterback Kirk Cousins, who was hit 7 times and sacked once during the game.

Robert Griffin III convinced about the San Francisco 49ers

The 49ers had wins against the LA Rams, Denver Broncos, Seattle Seahawks and the Dallas Cowboys to prove themselves to the rest of the league.

However, the Vikings were always going to pose a big challenge due to how dominant their defence has been this season. After the arrival of Cousins, many had them as one of the contenders for the Super Bowl, but with the 49ers having defeated them 35-10, they have now claimed a key status, according to Robert Griffin III.

"The San Francisco 49ers are the best team in the NFL. BY FAR," posted the former NFL quarterback.

With a 9-1 record, they are statistically the best team in the NFL. Both offensively and defensively, they have enough pieces to beat any side in the league, which is why they are definitely Super Bowl contenders.

With seven games remaining, the 49ers have matchups against the Seahawks, Rams, and the Kansas City Chiefs in the coming weeks. It will be interesting to see how the Kyle Shanahan-coached team overcomes these challenges, as that is what will determine whether they are actually real contenders for the Lombardi Trophy.

articles.title: Bengals-Commanders Monday Night Football betting odds, picks and predictions: Best bets, player props
articles.summary: Our NFL handicapper break downs his favorite bets in the Bengals-Commanders Monday Night Football matchup.
articles.body:
The top of the betting market's power ratings is like a hot nightclub.

The gatekeepers have something of a one-in, one-out policy, where there's only room for so many. But … if you're playing well enough, the limits will be pushed, and we'll find room for you.

After nine weeks of the NFL season, there were four teams considered a cut above:

Due to mediocre results, preseason lounge regulars — the Rams and Seahawks — have been left out in the coat room, while the Chiefs are always lingering in the front bar.

Then Joe Burrow and his crew showed up, blazing with a five-game winning streak, and an utter destruction of a division rival on prime time in Week 10.

The Bengals got their invite past the velvet rope, but now it's up to them to behave so as not to get bounced back out.

Cincinnati Bengals (-6.5, 53.5) at Washington Commanders

A week ago, the lookahead line for this matchup was Bengals -3.5, so there's a very easy measurement as to literally how much has changed after one game, since the Commanders' own Thursday Night Football win shouldn't have hurt the already-modest perception of Washington — three full points.

The Bengals offense has put up 30+ points in each of its last five games, but with a predominantly passing-centric offense, let's take a look at the pass defense metrics of their opponents, by Success Rate (adjusted for garbage time and high-leverage plays like turnovers and fourth downs):

After a season where the Commanders defense was a legitimate liability, they've quietly shown improvement, not allowing 30 points since Week 3, and the opponent Success Rate on dropbacks against Washington is 43.6% (seventh in the NFL).

One of those games was against fellow club member, and offensive equal, San Francisco, which carried a similar point spread of 49ers -6.5 in Week 6, but that was at home, and the Commanders got inside the number and then almost took the lead late.

The unfortunate part about getting into the betting market's VIP room, is that you're asked to perform at a high level to cash tickets for your bettors.

The Bills barely scraped over the 16.5 points required of them, while the Bears couldn't cover the 11.5-point spread they were favored by over the Saints, and the Jaguars were exposed by the Giants — the first functional team they've played in weeks. Of course, the 49ers (constants in the "club" by covering spreads at a high power rating) continued to prove they belong, crushing the Vikings 35-10 on Sunday night.

The other issue the Bengals' recent victims have had is that their offense had little chance of keeping up, even if they could slow Burrow in the passing game. Quarterbacks Tyler Huntley, Malik Willis, Cam Ward, Michael Penix Jr. and (advanced-age) Aaron Rodgers don't have the efficiency or second receiving threat that Jayden Daniels has.

Since returning from his early-season injury in Week 5, Daniels and the Commanders have an adjusted EPA/Play just behind the Cowboys and Broncos — and ahead of the Lions.

At home, still in divisional contention and on Monday night, look for this to be closer than you might think having seen Cincinnati in action last Sunday night.

Chase Brown under 46.5 rushing yards (-115, Bet365)

Brown is like a closer who is there to throw a changeup, like the Trevor Hoffman of running backs. However, if Cincinnati doesn't face the short-yardage situations it might have against the lesser defenses they've played of late, or have a big halftime lead, Brown's usage or efficiency might come down.

During the five-game winning streak, Brown topped out at 57 (with 36 yards on three carries in one second-half drive) and 55 yards (thanks to a meaningless, end-of-regulation carry for eight yards).

Tee Higgins over 5.5 receptions (+108, DraftKings)

The Commanders have struggled keeping the ball out of the hands of No. 1 receivers, as CeeDee Lamb, Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Puka Nacua combined for 32 receptions against Washington.

That might be a general point of emphasis for Dan Quinn, facing Ja'Marr Chase on Monday, but the problem is the Bengals have two top-tier wide receivers.

Tee Higgins' yardage totals have tailed off recently as Chase has had his way, but even as the second option, Higgins has five catches on six targets in a pair of blowouts. With a closer game, and more looks, he should get back to hauling in the 6+ catches he had in four of five before that.

Jayden Daniels over 223.5 passing yards (-113, FanDuel)

Whether it's as part of staying connected with the Bengals on the scoreboard, or trailing, if the game does start the way others have for Cincinnati opponents, Daniels should be spreading the ball around through the air.

Daniels has gone over this total in three of his last four games, with the other coming in a game with a division rival, the Eagles, where Philadelphia's offense didn't provide any kind of pressure to air it out.

Higgins was also held out of the end zone last week, after a run of five touchdowns in three previous games.

On his way to a third-straight 10+ touchdown season, scoring more often than not as long as Burrow is in the lineup, we'll take Higgins at around even-money.

Only the Lions allow more production (yardage and touchdowns) to opposing tight ends than the Commanders, and if there was one throw that Burrow would have liked to have back during an exquisite prime-time performance, it's the one he air-mailed by about 18 inches to Mike Gesicki in the back of the end zone. After five straight games with a score, back-to-back without one feels like a drought, but we know Gesicki will get a look or two.

RB Jacory Croskey-Merritt (+135, Bet365)

The Commanders also get their No. 1 runner back on Monday, and maybe, David Blough will shift away from his the torturous goal-line play-calling we were subjected to against the Giants, with a tailback he's more comfortable handing the ball to in those situations?

Jacory Croskey-Merritt is coming off IR for the first time since an 11-carry, 82-yard performance, with a touchdown in Week 5, so we'll assume he's getting the primary role back.

In his rookie season, "Bill" had eight rushing touchdowns, so that's 10 in 22 career games.

No team has allowed more yards per catch to the tight end position than the Bengals, and (eventually) that translated to a Pat Freiermuth touchdown last week. With four explosive catches, that's one shy of the team lead for Washington, so this might be as good an opportunity as Okonkwo has had all season to get his first touchdown.

The ball was briefly in Burks' hands at the end of the aforementioned game with the 49ers, but he hasn't scored since getting in the end zone in two of his first three games this season.

Burks' size (6-foot-2, 225 pounds) makes him a different type of option in the red zone, compared to the other receivers — Stefon Diggs and Antonio Williams — who are under six feet and less than 200 lbs.

Not scoring recently lengthens Burks' odds, while a high game total suggests anyone is a little more likely to score than usual, creating value on a longer shot.

articles.title: Is Joe Burrow having the best season ever for an NFL quarterback?
articles.summary: Breaking down the incredible all-time numbers for the Bengals' red-hot QB.
articles.body:
Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow will win his first NFL MVP award in 2026. Unless he suffers another unfortunate injury from now through the end of the regular season or Cincinnati freefalls from the AFC playoffs, that is one lock in an unpredictable year.

Burrow has put up big numbers for an offense that heavily relies on the pass and because of it, the Bengals (7-2) stand strongly in first place in the tough AFC North, going into Monday night's Week 11 finale at Washington.

Thanks to his dominant, healthy campaign, the Bengals should end a four-year playoff drought and earn their third division title over the past six seasons with Burrow at QB.

Burrow would become the seventh player to win both the Heisman Trophy, college's top individual honor, and NFL MVP, joining Cam Newton, Lamar Jackson and others. He would become the 11th No. 1 overall pick to win NFL MVP, joining Newton, Matthew Stafford and others.

Should the Bengals go all the way, Burrow would become the first player in football history to win the Heisman, a college national championship, get drafted No. 1 overall, win NFL MVP and also win a Super Bowl.

Burrow's 2019 historic season at LSU is considered among the best-ever among college QBs. That year, he completed 76.3 percent of his passes for 5,671 yards and 60 TDs in 15 games. He averaged 10.8 yards per attempt, 378.1 yards per game and would have rated a ridiculous 143.7 using the NFL efficiency model.

Although Burrow — and maybe no other QB at any other level — will never match those special numbers, there's a case that Burrow is also having the greatest NFL passing season by a quarterback in the modern era. With his 2026 Bengals stats, here is how he stacks up with Hall of Fame greats across the board.

Breaking down Joe Burrow's 2026 passing stats

Drew Brees' record: 74.4 with the Saints in 2018

Burrow is besting Brees here while matching him in averaging 8.2 yards per attempt. Brees didn't break 4,000 passing yards. In his 15 games, he was capped at 32 touchdown passes, or five more than Burrow has in nine games.

Brees had that completion percentage while averaging 32.6 attempts per game. Burrow, with the Bengals calling for 64.8 percent passing, is averaging 37.8. He doesn't have much margin for error to break Brees' record, but Burrow is showing off his accuracy with significantly higher volume.

Peyton Manning's record: 5,477 with the Broncos in 2013

Manning did this in 16 games vs. 17. He averaged 342.3 passing yards per game, while Burrow is averaging a still-impressive 310.6. Manning got there by averaging 8.3 yards per attempt, or slightly more than Burrow in '26 and Brees in '18.

Another thing: Manning averaged 41.2 passing attempts per game, well more than Burrow. He had 659 attempts that season. Burrow is on pace for 642 over 17 games. Going with that 8.3 yards per attempt, Manning would have 5,338, still more than Burrow. This is pretty close and this number doesn't mean as much as the others.

Peyton Manning's record: 55 with the Broncos in 2013

An extra game on the schedule helps Burrow. Manning hit 55 in 16 games that season, averaging 3.44 TD passes per game. Burrow is right at averaging 3 TD passes per game, with 27 in 9 games. Burrow would need to average 3.5 TD passes per game the rest of the way in the final 8 games to get to 55.

That means he needs to have at least four games with 4 or more TD passes and match that with four games throwing 3 TD passes. That's not an unreasonable hot finish to the season, but Burrow needs to become extra prolific down the stretch to surpass Manning's mark. For now, Burrow would likely be settling for being the fourth member of the 50-TD club, joining Manning, Tom Brady and Patrick Mahomes.

Manning set the passing yards and passing TDs records in the same season. In doing so, he completed 68.3 of his passes, well fewer than Burrow.

Aaron Rodgers' record: 122.5 with the Packers in 2011

The Rodgers' number is incredible. He averaged 309.5 passing yards per game that season with a robust 9.2 yards per attempt. He had 45 TDs to only 6 interceptions. Burrow is at 27 TDs with 6 INTs. Burrow needs to keep racking up TDs while keeping the INTs down. He also needs some bigger plays downfield to push his yards per attempt upward.

Burrow isn't right behind Rodgers here, as he ranks sixth behind Rodgers twice with the Packers, Manning in '04 with the Colts , Lamar Jackson in '24 with the Ravens and Nick Foles in 2013 with the Eagles . Considering Burrow's other numbers, this is a hyper-efficient number for him.

Tom Brady's record: 490 with the Buccaneers in 2022

Brady set this record at age 45 in his final season with his second team, playing a full 17 games. He averaged 28.8 completions per game. Burrow is right behind that pace through nine games, at 28.2 completions per game. This number is well within reach, as Burrow needs to average 29.6 completions per game over the final eight games to break the record

There have been many great quarterback passing seasons. There's also Jackson's special dual-threat explosion in 2024. In that year, to earn his second MVP with the Ravens, Jackson passed for 41 TDs at 8.8 yards per attempt while rating 119.6, the last two numbers higher than Burrow. Jackson also added 915 rushing yards while averaging a league-leading 6.6 yards per attempt.

Manning led the Broncos to the Super Bowl after his '13 season. Brees in '18 and Brady in '22 didn't get to the Super Bowl with their record seasons. Jackson's '24 team lost in the divisional round to Josh Allen's Bills . Rodgers' '11 team was also famously upset by Eli Manning's Giants in the same round.

For Burrow's season to separate and get unquestioned status as best-ever, he must parlay his play to a second Super Bowl trip. Winning Super Bowl 61 would put him in a category all by himself.

articles.title: Josh Allen is 'Scariest Player Ever,' Says Rival NFL Exec, 'I Don't Even Know Why He Throws'
articles.summary: Buffalo Bills star quarterback Josh Allen continues to strike fear into opponents after helping his team improve to 9-1 with Sunday's 26-9 win over the Miami Dolphins.
articles.body:
Buffalo Bills star quarterback Josh Allen continues to strike fear into opponents after helping his team improve to 9-1 with Sunday's 26-9 win over the Miami Dolphins.

The Athletic's Mike Sando spoke to an executive from a Bills opponent who spoke glowingly of Allen and his running skills.

"He is the scariest player ever," the exec said. "I don't even know why he throws the ball. Every time he throws it, you're grateful, because he could run for 20 yards every play. He can take over a game. Now, part of the problem is, it is hero ball."

Surprisingly, Allen didn't use his legs in Sunday's game against the Dolphins. He completed 27 of his 45 passes for 304 yards, a touchdown and two interceptions while getting sacked three times. Still, Buffalo never lost control of the game after jumping out to a 20-6 lead in the first half.

Even without relying on his dual-threat abilities on Sunday, Allen is still tied for second in the NFL with 11 rushing touchdowns this season. The 30-year-old appears extra motivated to help the Bills finally break through and reach the Super Bowl this year.

Allen and the Bills will face a tougher test when they meet the Kansas City Chiefs (8-2) in a primetime matchup on Thanksgiving Day.
